items.title: World Cup-winner Petit joins call for change in FIFA leadership
items.description: Several ex-footballers, including Premier League winners Emmanuel Petit and Mikael Silvestre, have called for “change” in FIFA’s leadership following the failed plan to open the World Cup to private investors. “Change is necessary. Power has blurred the current leadership’s ability to distinguish between its own interests and what is best for football,” Frenchmen Silvestre, Petit and Olivier Dacourt said in social media posts. The ex-players did not directly mention FIFA president Gianni Infantino, who earlier in the day was backed by former Barcelona star Samuel Eto’o, but they criticised his leadership. “We share exactly the same concerns as millions of supporters around the world. Like them, we have watched the sport we love drift away from its core values under FIFA’s current leadership,” the former players said. They also did not directly refer to the behind-the-scenes negotiations conducted by Infantino to place World Cup revenues into a commercial company open to private investors — a plan that was abandoned this summer under pressure from the European, North American and Asian confederations. Petit won the World Cup with France in 1998 and also won French and English titles with Monaco and Arsenal. Silvestre, who sits on a FIFA anti-racism panel, was a five-time Premier League winner with Manchester United and part of the French squad that reached the 2006 World Cup final. Under-fire Infantino remains determined to seek another term when FIFA holds its next presidential election in Rabat next March. AFP The post World Cup-winner Petit joins call for change in FIFA leadership appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Govt increases petrol price by Rs0.39, high-speed diesel by Rs2.40
items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · "> The government on Monday raised the price of petrol by Rs0.39 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.40 per litre. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs341.98 per litre while HSD will cost Rs370.69 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on August 25. The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: Colombia’s new president orders migrant deportations
items.description: Colombia’s right-wing President Abelardo de la Espriella has ordered a crackdown on irregular migration, instructing authorities to begin detaining undocumented foreigners convicted of crimes with a view to deporting them. The hardline lawyer took office on August 7 with an agenda to fight crime and drug-trafficking guerrillas. Irregular migration was not a central theme of his campaign but in video footage of him chairing a security meeting in his Caribbean stronghold of Barranquilla on Sunday, he said: “I will not accept illegal migrants, no matter where they come from.” “The order to Immigration (authorities) is clear: first those who are committing crimes, second those who have not regularized their status and who will have to be deported in due course.” He said deportation procedures would start this week by presidential order. It was not immediately clear that time-frame referred to Barranquilla, Colombia’s fourth-largest city, or to the wider country. – ‘Colombians first’ – Colombia has been the main port of call for Venezuelans fleeing the economic crisis across the border in their country over the past decade. According to Colombia’s immigration department, 2.8 million Venezuelans were living in Colombia as of June of this year. Of these, more than 527,000 are undocumented. Previous right-wing leaders have been tolerant of Venezuelan migrants, seeing them as victims of the socialist policies of ousted president Nicolas Maduro and his firebrand predecessor Hugo Chavez. Prior to the crisis in Venezuela, Colombia had been a country of emigration rather than immigration, with six decades of armed conflict sending millions fleeing abroad. In his first days in office, which coincided with a powerful earthquake that left over 300 people dead in western Colombia, De la Espriella cast himself as a unifier. In Sunday’s meeting, however, he echoed the “America First” agenda of US President Donald Trump, of whom he is an avid fan. “Colombians, first, Colombians second, Colombians third, may that be clear to everyone,” De la Espriella said. AFP The post Colombia’s new president orders migrant deportations appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: CDF Munir vows continued efforts to stabilise region in meeting with Iran’s Ghalibaf
items.description: Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir met Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf in Tehran on Monday during his visit to the Iranian capital, according to Iranian state broadcaster Press TV . The CDF and interior minister reached Tehran earlier today, Iranian media reported , after Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) described the visit “as part of Pakistan’s efforts to promote regional peace and stability”. According to the Iranian broadcaster, Ghalibaf reaffirmed Tehran’s commitment to upholding the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, while criticising the United States for failing to honour its commitments. He said this approach had “hindered regional stability and further eroded trust in Washington”. Field Marshal Munir said Pakistan would continue its efforts to help restore stability in the region, Press TV reported. Later, Mohsen Rezaei, the secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, expressed his distrust of Washington during a meeting with Field Marshal Munir, according to the Fars news agency. “America must change its behaviour and take practical actions regarding the implementation of the conditions of the agreement,” Rezaei was quoted as saying by Fars . Iranian news agency ISNA has also published photographs of a meeting between Field Marshal Munir and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian. Earlier today, CDF Munir and Naqvi met with Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni in Tehran, state media in Pakistan reported. Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said that the visit undertaken by CDF Munir and Naqvi was taking place as bilateral ties between Islamabad and Tehran “reach one of their strongest stages”, state broadcaster IRIB reported. Baqaei added that the Pakistani delegation’s visit was unrelated to the visit of Oman’s foreign minister, who is expected to arrive today. He noted that “both visits will address regional security issues”. ISPR said CDF Munir will “focus on promoting efforts towards peaceful, lasting and comprehensive resolution of the conflict in the Middle East” during the visit. Baqaei on Sunday said CDF Munir was expected to travel to Tehran to continue efforts to bring peace and security to the region. He said CDF Munir would lead an official delegation and the “visit aims to strengthen bilateral cooperation between Iran and Pakistan and to continue Pakis­tan’s good offices in support of peace and security in the region”. During the visit, CDF Munir would meet and hold talks with senior officials Iran, Baqaei added. The United States and Israel triggered the Middle East war with a massive wave of strikes against Iran on February 28, triggering Iranian retaliation across the region. An April 8 ceasefire ended nearly 40 days of intense bombardment, but control over the Strait of Hormuz soon emerged as a key flashpoint in the conflict. Iran has controlled the vital energy conduit since the war began. Reopening the strait, vital for global oil and gas supplies, has become a US priority, but Tehran insists the waterway will remain closed until Washington lifts its naval blockade on Iranian ports, removes oil sanctions and unfreezes Iranian assets abroad. Pakistan has played a key role in efforts to halt war between Iran and the United States, brokering a memorandum of understanding (MoU) in June, but peace negotiations currently appear stalled. Last week, US President Donald Trump announced that Washington would ramp up economic pressure on Iran “on an unprecedented scale”. Washington has urged other governments, including Beijing, to join efforts to further isolate Iran’s economy. The US is expected to announce details related to the planned sanctions on Mondau, which ​US officials have ​said would be “ the ⁠toughest sanctions in history ” on Iran. Additional input from AFP

items.title: Joint opposition announces strategy against economic crisis, political repression
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The joint opposition held its first parliamentary meeting at Parliament House on Monday and announced a collective strategy to address violence, the economic crisis and political repression. The meeting was attended by opposition party leaders, including Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, National Assembly Opposition Leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai, Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas Jafri, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and others. Speaking at a press conference after the meeting, the JUI-F chief said opposition parties had agreed to play a joint role in parliament and stressed that collective strategies and actions would be pursued through mutual consultation. He said it was not the time to divide the provinces, warning that such a move would only increase mistrust among the federating units. “We completely agree that this is absolutely not the time to divide the provinces; neither is the environment conducive to it nor is there any prior preparation.” “Dividing the provinces will increase unrest,” he said, claiming that the 18th Amendment had become a “thorn in the throat” of the establishment. He said all opposition parties agreed that Pakistan, at the state level, could not afford the prevailing situation. “People are also on the streets in Kashmir,” he said, alleging that violence was being used instead of addressing public grievances. Fazl also called for the release of prisoners and the creation of a positive political environment. He described the day as a “blessed day” and said lawmakers sitting on the opposition benches had decided to act as a joint opposition. “We are together today in view of the law and order situation in the country,” he said. “On one side, our land is red with blood, while on the other, our rulers are walking on red carpets during foreign tours.” He said the deteriorating law and order situation was also severely affecting the national economy. Referring to Pakistan’s rivalry with India, he said the two countries often talked about war and competition, while India had now become the world’s fourth-largest economy. He also questioned Pakistan’s standing in international judicial rankings. Addressing the press conference, Achakzai said the opposition’s unity was a positive development, adding that opposition members had reached an agreement despite the “suffocating atmosphere” in parliament. “It is a day of happiness and facilitation,” he said, expressing hope that the alliance would play an important role in restoring Pakistan’s lost glory. “Today, there is unrest and bloodshed across the country, with more than 100 people losing their lives every day, yet no one seems to be paying any attention. “The Constitution clearly lays down the procedure for creating provinces. In contrast, creating provinces through an executive order, in the same way that districts are created, would amount to an attack on the foundations of Pakistan. “We warn those forces that if you do so, you will not be able to stop the people of Pakistan, and everyone will take to the streets. Pakistan can no longer afford to tolerate such circumstances,” he asserted. “The poor are crying out for food, people are worried about employment, children are being deprived of basic necessities, and the education system is being ruined,” he said. Meanwhile, Abbas said the opposition’s unity during the month marking the birth of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was a good sign. “We are cultivating enmities instead of friendships,” he alleged, adding that the lives of citizens were not secure. He also alleged that the sanctity of the home and the privacy of families were being violated and said that the honour and dignity of citizens were not protected. Referring to the condition of incarcerated PTI leader Dr Yasmin Rashid, he said her situation was known to everyone. He also claimed that the Supreme Court had ordered the transfer of PTI founder Imran Khan to Shifa International Hospital, but alleged that the law and judicial decisions were being ignored. Barrister Gohar said leaders of opposition parties had met and agreed to remain united. “All opposition parties will adopt a common position in parliament,” he said, adding that they would speak with one voice on law and order, inflation and Pakistan’s relations with other countries. He said the PTI had assured the JUI-F that it would give it full support. On the question of provincial restructuring, he said no constitutional amendment concerning the provinces could be made overnight, stressing the need for consultation and consensus.

items.title: 24-hour market: Who is actually in charge?
items.description: Ghanaians deserve a straight answer to a simple question: who owns the 24-Hour Markets Project? Because right now, we have three different stories. What is being built: Since January this year, the government has been rolling out “24-Hour Economy Markets” across the country, starting with 11 municipalities and districts in the Upper West Region alone. These projects have been publicly branded, launched, and defended as flagship deliveries under the 24-Hour Economy agenda, the same agenda this government swept into office promising in 2024. What the programme document actually says: The 24H+ Programme document, the Presidency’s own 287-page blueprint for the 24-Hour Economy, makes exactly ONE specific commitment to round-the-clock markets: 24/7 fish markets, under the fisheries value chain (GROW24). There is no broad, costed, cross-cutting commitment in that document to build 24-hour markets nationwide. Yet market construction has been marketed to the public as central to this same programme. What the Presidential Adviser is now saying: On August 19, Mr. Goosie Tanoh, the Presidential Adviser on the 24-Hour Economy, told the press, “The 24-Hour Markets Project is not our responsibility. We are not into development of markets. We don’t know anything about that.” He went further, revealing his outfit has been named in lawsuits over market demolitions and is now moving to get the secretariat’s name off those suits, insisting the project belongs to the Ministry of Local Government and is funded through the District Assemblies Common Fund. Our question to Ghanaians is simple: If the 24-Hour Economy Secretariat has “no jurisdiction” over 24-hour markets, why has this project been marketed under the 24-Hour Economy brand for over a year? Who authorised the demolitions communities are now suing over? Which budget line, which ministry, and which minister are actually accountable for these markets, and do Parliament and the Public Accounts and Finance Committees have visibility into how District Assemblies Common Fund resources are being applied to this project? The government cannot claim the political credit for “24-Hour Markets” as a signature delivery of its flagship programme, and then have its own chief adviser disown it the moment demolitions and lawsuits land on the table Ghanaians were promised transformation. They deserve to know who is actually driving it.

items.title: OSP’s swift response to extortion allegation doesn’t mean selective investigations – Senanu
items.description: Anti-corruption campaigner Edem Senanu has defended the Office of the Special Prosecutor’s (OSP) swift response to an alleged extortion case made by the Chief Executive of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), Sammy Gyamfi, against the Minority Leader of Parliament, Alexander Afenyo-Markin, arguing that the speed of its reaction does not suggest the anti-corruption agency is selective in deciding which matters to investigate. His comments follow concerns over what some observers perceive as a difference in the OSP’s handling of the extortion allegation and the bribery case involving Aksa Energy. Mr Senanu explained that the two cases cannot be directly compared, particularly because the Aksa Energy matter involved a long-running investigation in collaboration with United States authorities. According to him, the OSP would have been constrained from publicly disclosing details of its involvement in the case while investigations by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) were ongoing. He noted that investigations of that nature are often conducted confidentially to prevent suspects from becoming aware of investigative strategies or taking steps to evade prosecution. “It’s not about picking and choosing,” Mr Senanu said, explaining that the Aksa Energy case was a collaborative international investigation that had reportedly lasted several years before becoming public. He argued that the OSP’s role in such a process was necessarily different from its response to a locally reported allegation brought directly to its attention. Mr Senanu said specialised investigative agencies such as the OSP may need to do more public education about how investigations are conducted, particularly when cases involve international partners. “If the FBI is investigating something and collaborating with you, they don’t tell you not to put anything out,” he explained, stressing that premature disclosure could undermine an ongoing case. He added that investigators must sometimes protect the confidentiality of their work to ensure that suspects do not have the opportunity to frustrate the process. On the extortion allegation, Mr Senanu said the matter is local and has been brought to the attention of the OSP, making it reasonable for the office to indicate that it is assessing whether it can investigate. He therefore rejected suggestions that the OSP’s prompt response amounted to selective enforcement. The debate over the OSP’s approach comes amid renewed scrutiny of the anti-corruption agency’s handling of high-profile allegations and calls for greater consistency and transparency in the fight against corruption. Mr Senanu maintained that differences in the timing and manner of public responses should not, on their own, be interpreted as evidence that the OSP is deliberately choosing which cases to pursue.

items.title: Africa risks missing tech revolution without human capital — Jonathan
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — Former President Goodluck Jonathan has warned that Africa risks missing out on the current technological revolution unless urgent steps are taken to strengthen human capital development across the continent. Jonathan gave the warning on Monday while delivering a lecture titled, “Harnessing Industrial Capacity for Inclusive Growth and Regional Stability in Africa,” to participants of Course 34 of the National Defence College in Abuja. He said Africa’s abundant natural resources alone could not guarantee prosperity without the capacity to convert them into high-value goods and services. “If we miss out on the industrial revolution, agri-revolution, all the revolutions, ICT is now ruling the world. We cannot continue to lag behind. We must focus on young people,” he said. The former President noted that Africa had abundant natural resources, a large market and significant human capital but continued to lag behind other regions in industrialisation and value addition. He said technological development should form a central component of Africa’s industrialisation strategy, noting that knowledge, innovation and technology were increasingly driving the world’s wealthiest economies. Jonathan said transforming Africa’s education and industrial sectors would require sustained political commitment and determination. “We cannot achieve that overnight, but with a commitment by the leaders, a determination by the citizens, we can still change the story of Africa,” he said. He expressed concern over the performance of African universities in global rankings, describing the situation as a major challenge to the continent’s technological and industrial advancement. According to him, meaningful technological development and industrialisation would remain difficult without a stronger education system and specialised institutions capable of producing the skilled manpower required to drive innovation. Jonathan said African countries needed to review their education systems from the primary level through university education and place greater emphasis on specialised training. “We must review and recalibrate our businesses from the primary schools to the universities. We don’t have any specialised universities in Africa. It’s terribly bad,” he said. He urged African leaders to prioritise investment in education and human capital, stressing that the knowledge and skills of young people were among the continent’s most valuable resources. Citing Singapore as an example, Jonathan said the country’s transformation into a globally competitive economy was supported by deliberate investment in education and capacity building. He also cited India’s emergence as a major player in information technology, attributing its progress partly to the establishment of specialised institutions designed to develop highly skilled manpower. “India, at independence from the British, set up institutions that prepared India for the future. They set up specialised institutions, not for everybody. They are training their best brains to control and dominate the world,” he said. Jonathan urged African countries to move beyond an education system focused primarily on producing graduates and instead develop institutions that promote innovation and specialised skills in science, technology, engineering and information technology. He also urged the graduating participants of the National Defence College, whom he described as emerging strategic leaders, to champion policies that would strengthen education, technological capacity and industrial development in their respective countries. items.title: FGF : une Assemblée générale extraordinaire et élective convoquée le 27 octobre, à Conakry
items.description: La Fédération Guinéenne de Football (FGF) a officiellement annoncé ce lundi 24 août, la tenue de son Assemblée générale extraordinaire et élective, conformément aux dispositions de l'article 29.8 de ses Statuts. Cette importante session est prévue le mardi 27 octobre 2026 à 10h00 GMT, à Conakry. Selon le communiqué, l'ordre du jour portera sur l'élection du président, des vice-présidents et des membres du Comité exécutif de la FGF pour un mandat de quatre ans. La Fédération précise que cette session élective est convoquée « à la suite de la vacance de plus de cinquante pour cent (50 %) des postes au sein du Comité exécutif », en application de l'article 36.9 des Statuts. Un processus encadré par les textes La FGF assure que le scrutin se déroulera « dans le strict respect des Statuts, du Code électoral et des autres textes réglementaires applicables ». Les opérations électorales seront supervisées par la Commission électorale de la Fédération, conformément à l'article 60.1 des Statuts. Les candidatures devront être déposées « dans les formes, conditions et délais prévus par les textes applicables » avant leur examen et leur validation par les organes électoraux compétents. Renouveler les instances dirigeantes Dans son communiqué, la Fédération invite l'ensemble des membres de l'Assemblée générale à prendre les dispositions nécessaires afin d'assurer leur participation effective à cette session, qu'elle qualifie d'« étape majeure dans le processus de renouvellement des instances dirigeantes ». La FGF réaffirme enfin son engagement à garantir un processus électoral « régulier, transparent, inclusif et conforme à ses textes statutaires et réglementaires ». items.title: Sudan anti-war forces reject El Burhan dialogue call
items.description: Sudanese anti-war civilian and political forces have rejected Sovereignty Council President and Commander-in-Chief of the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) Lt Gen Abdelfattah El Burhan’s call for political dialogue, arguing that no credible political process can take place while the war continues. The position was renewed at the end of a two-day meeting in Ethiopia’s capital of Addis Ababa , where political parties, including the forces behind the “Sudanese Declaration of Principles”, the Popular Congress Party, the Umma Party, civil society organisations, and feminist and youth networks agreed that Sudan needs a genuine peace process focused on stopping the fighting and addressing the humanitarian crisis. The participants described El Burhan’s dialogue call as a political manoeuvre aimed at consolidating the army’s authority, granting it political legitimacy and paving the way for elements of the former regime and the Islamic movement to return to power. The participants adopted a joint position paper, The Peace Process We Want , calling for an independent political process free from the dominance of either party to the conflict and rejecting dialogue that could entrench military rule. Former Prime Minister and Civil Democratic Alliance of Revolutionary Forces (Sumoud) president Abdalla Hamdok described the Addis Ababa gathering as a major development for Sudan’s civilian forces. He said the meeting had disproved expectations that the civilian camp could not unite. Despite the scale of the country’s crisis, Hamdok said “hope is there” and urged continued efforts to overcome the conditions that have prolonged the war. The anti-war forces reaffirmed their support for the Quadrilateral Roadmap issued in September 2025 and called for a unified international mediation framework. Their proposed action plan includes measures for the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) to de-escalate the conflict and agree to an immediate truce. Participants also agreed to form a joint committee to coordinate the positions and vision of the anti-war civilian camp. The meeting concluded with an appeal to Sudanese people at home and abroad to reject the war, confront hate speech and polarisation, and work towards a comprehensive peace that restores civilian authority and preserves Sudan’s unity. items.title: Ebola en RDC: Léon XIV appelle à une mobilisation internationale renforcée
items.description: Le pape Léon XIV a appelé, le dimanche 23 août 2026, à une intensification de la solidarité internationale face à l’épidémie d’Ebola qui sévit en République démocratique du Congo (RDC). Selon Vatican News, le souverain pontife a, également, insisté sur la nécessité d’associer davantage les communautés locales aux efforts de prévention. Le pape Léon XIV tire la sonnette d’alarme face à la progression de l’épidémie d’Ebola en République démocratique du Congo. Dans un appel rendu public, le dimanche 23 août 2026, le souverain pontife a exhorté la communauté internationale à renforcer son soutien à la riposte sanitaire engagée dans le pays. Selon les données communiquées par le ministère congolais de la Santé et rapportées par Vatican News, l’épidémie a déjà fait 2 557 morts sur 5 375 cas confirmés. La transmission du virus demeure active dans 56 zones de santé, avec une situation particulièrement préoccupante en Ituri. L’appel du pape porte également sur la participation des populations locales aux actions de prévention. «J’encourage une réaction de la communauté internationale qui implique également les communautés locales dans les actions de prévention, afin de sauver de nombreuses vies humaines», a déclaré Léon XIV. Cette nouvelle flambée est liée à la souche Bundibugyo du virus Ebola. Il s’agit de la 17e épidémie enregistrée en RDC depuis la découverte de la maladie dans le pays. Face à la persistance de la transmission, l’Organisation mondiale de la santé (OMS) et le Centre africain de contrôle et de prévention des maladies (Africa CDC) plaident eux aussi pour un renforcement de la riposte et de l’appui international. Sur le plan vaccinal, Kinshasa a réceptionné plus de 16 000 doses du vaccin Ervebo. Toutefois, ce vaccin étant homologué contre une autre souche du virus Ebola, son utilisation dans le contexte actuel demeure limitée. La riposte sanitaire est, par ailleurs, confrontée à un autre obstacle majeur: l’insécurité. Les violences armées qui persistent dans plusieurs provinces de l’Est de la RDC compliquent l’accès des équipes médicales aux populations touchées et perturbent les opérations de surveillance, de prévention et de prise en charge. Alors que la propagation du virus se poursuit, les autorités congolaises, soutenues par leurs partenaires sanitaires, appellent à une mobilisation accrue. L’objectif reste de freiner la transmission de la maladie et de limiter au maximum les pertes en vies humaines, dans un contexte où la solidarité internationale apparaît plus que jamais déterminante Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Ebola en RDC: Léon XIV appelle à une mobilisation internationale renforcée est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Maradona’s ‘Hand of God’ ball sells for £2.5m
items.description: The football with which Diego Maradona scored his famous ‘hand of God’ goal at the 1986 World Cup has sold at auction for £2.5m. Maradona famously punched the ball past goalkeeper Peter Shilton in Argentina’s 2-1 quarter-final win over England. After the game, he told reporters it had been scored “a little with the head of Maradona and a little with the hand of God”. Maradona later scored what became known as the ‘goal of the century’ in the same game, dribbling past five England outfield players before slotting the ball past Shilton. Though it sold for $3.3m (£2.5m) at Heritage Auctions in the United States on Saturday, the ball had been expected to fetch nearer $10m (£7.3m). Speaking to Reuters before the auction, Mike Provenzale, a specialist auctioneer at Heritage, said: “It’s a true one-of-one item. Arguably the most significant soccer item that exists.” Tunisian Ali Bin Nasser, who refereed the match in 1986, collected the Adidas Azteca ball at full-time and kept it for more than three decades. In 2023, he signed a letter to confirm it was the only ball used during the match, which has also been confirmed by further independent authentication. Bin Nasser sold the ball in 2022 for $2.37m (£1.74m). Its new owner again put it up for auction in 2023 though it did not sell as bids did not meet the minimum value set. Reacting to Yari’s confidence in Tinubu’s re-election and the APC’s continued dominance beyond 2027, Abdullahi said the senator was defending his new role. “He’s one of those lying to the President,” Abdullahi said. “We understand he needs to justify his new appointment,” he added. Abdullahi also criticised the APC while comparing it with the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), recalling the PDP’s past claim that it would remain in power for decades. “But what happened? At least, the PDP was a real political party, not this SPV (Special Purpose Vehicle),” he said. Yari had expressed confidence that Tinubu would secure re-election in 2027 and that the APC would remain in power beyond the President’s possible second term. The ADC spokesman, however, dismissed the ruling party’s political prospects, arguing that the 2027 elections would provide an opportunity for Nigerians to assess the competing political parties and their candidates. items.description: Ghana Women’s Premier League champions, Ampem Darkoa Ladies, enjoyed a winning start to the 2026 WAFU B Women’s Champions League Qualifiers. Ampem Darkoa Ladies recorded a 1-0 win over defending champions ASEC Mimosas in their opening game of the competition. Gloria Adomako scored the only goal of the game in the first half to ensure all three points for the Nana Mma. The Ivorian side came close to scoring g the opening goal in the sixth minute but failed to get their effort on target from the penalty spot. Goalkeeper Rose Baah made a brilliant save to deny the Ivorians to keep the score at 0-0. Zakaria Ajegipina and Nancy Amoh also came close to breaking the deadlock but their attempts to catch the goalkeeper other lines both failed to find the back of the net. However, there was no denying Adomako in the 29th minute as she headed home the first goal for Ampem Darkoa. Loanee Milot Pokuaa also came close to doubling the lead for the Techiman-based team after the recess but her shot from close range came off the upright. In between the Milot chance and the closing stages of the game, Baah made some good saves to deny ASEC an equaliser in the game as Ampem Darkoa Ladies went on to secure all three points. items.title: Ayyoub Bouaddi va devenir le joueur le plus cher vendu par un club de Ligue 1
items.description: Ayyoub Bouaddi est sur le point d’entrer dans l’histoire du football français. Le jeune milieu de terrain marocain de Lille, âgé de seulement 18 ans, devrait rejoindre Manchester City pour 100 millions d’euros, faisant de lui la plus grosse vente de l’histoire de la Ligue 1 vers un club étranger. L’accord entre Lille et Manchester City, annoncé ces derniers jours, pourrait ainsi permettre au LOSC de réaliser une opération exceptionnelle avec l’un des plus grands espoirs du football marocain. Dimanche, alors que Lille affrontait Angers en championnat, Bouaddi était bien présent avec le groupe nordiste pour le déplacement en Anjou. Pourtant, le jeune international marocain n’a pas participé à la rencontre, remportée 2-0 par Lille, et ne figurait même pas sur la feuille de match. Selon L’Équipe , Bouaddi a passé une partie de l’après-midi à patienter dans le hall menant à la pelouse du stade Raymond-Kopa. Une situation particulière alors que son avenir semblait déjà se dessiner loin du Nord de la France. À seulement 18 ans, le milieu de terrain s’apprête en effet à franchir un immense cap en rejoignant Manchester City. Le montant de l’opération, 100 millions d’euros bonus compris, ferait de Bouaddi le joueur le plus cher jamais vendu par un club de Ligue 1 à l’étranger. Son départ vers Manchester City devrait désormais lui permettre de poursuivre sa progression au sein d’un effectif habitué à jouer les premiers rôles en Angleterre et en Europe. À Manchester City, le jeune milieu devra désormais franchir une nouvelle étape et gagner progressivement sa place dans un effectif particulièrement compétitif. items.title: Zawiya El Hadj Malick Sy de Dakar: plus d’un siècle d’histoire, entre dans une nouvelle ère
items.description: Fermée depuis le 9 janvier dernier, la Zawiya El Hadj Malick Sy, située sur l’avenue Lamine Guèye à Dakar, a été finalement rasée, marquant ainsi le lancement effectif des travaux de reconstruction de cet important édifice religieux tidiane. Cette opération s’inscrit dans le vaste projet de rénovation initié par le Khalife général des Tidianes, Serigne Babacar Sy Mansour, en vue de redonner à ce haut lieu spirituel son lustre d’antan, après plusieurs décennies d’existence. L’annonce de la réhabilitation avait été faite le 3 janvier dernier, à l’occasion du Gamou annuel de la Zawiya, par Serigne Mame Ousmane Sy Habib, envoyé spécial du Khalife général. Il avait alors souligné la nécessité de préserver la mémoire spirituelle et culturelle de ce site emblématique pour les générations futures. Selon les responsables du projet, les travaux ont été confiés à l’association Jama Atoun Nour Assouniya, sous la conduite de Mouhamadou Makhtar Cissé, pour assurer la reconstruction de l’édifice dans le respect de son identité religieuse et architecturale. En attendant l’achèvement des travaux, les activités religieuses – notamment les cinq prières quotidiennes, la Wazifa et la Hadaratoul Djumah – sont transférées provisoirement à la mosquée de la rue Blanchot, dirigée par l’imam Rawane Mbaye. À l’origine, une modeste case… Zawiya remonte au début du XXe siècle. En 1905, elle n’était qu’une simple case. Une baraque en bois y fut édifiée en 1909, avant d’être remplacée en 1927 par un modeste bâtiment en dur. En 1975, un grand édifice fut construit à l’initiative d’El Hadji Djily Mbaye, en accord avec l’imam ratib de l’époque, El Hadji Seydou Diop, et sur autorisation de feu El Hadji Abdoul Aziz Sy, alors Khalife général des Tidianes. Fondée par le Cheikh El Hadj Malick Sy, la Zawiya El Hadj Malick Sy demeure l’une des principales institutions de la Tidjaniya au Sénégal. Elle constitue un centre de rayonnement religieux et spirituel, accueillant depuis des décennies fidèles et étudiants en sciences islamiques venus du pays et de l’étranger. À travers cet acte, Tivaouane entend ainsi préserver ce patrimoine symbolique et lui permettre de continuer à jouer un rôle central dans la vie religieuse et culturelle de la capitale sénégalaise. Salla GUEYE

items.title: We will take action against Sammy Gyamfi over false allegations against Afenyo-Markin — Suame MP vows
items.description: Member of Parliament for Suame, John Darko, has rejected allegations levelled against the Minority Leader, Alexander Afenyo-Markin, by the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), Sammy Gyamfi. Mr Gyamfi had made extortion claims against Mr Afenyo-Markin in a war of words following the latter’s demand for accountability over a reported $1.7 billion loss involving the government’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme (DGPP) He said Mr Afenyo-Markin had never extorted Mr Gyamfi or any other person and described the Minority Leader as a “genuine-hearted” and “blameless” politician who was committed to serving the country. Mr Darko said the Minority Caucus would take legal action against the GoldBod CEO over what he described as false allegations against the Effutu MP. “We will take action against this guy for all the lies because, look, nothing like that has happened,” he said. Mr Darko was speaking on Joy FM’s Top Story on Monday, August 24, 2026, in reaction to the claims made by Mr Gyamfi concerning Mr Afenyo-Markin. The Suame MP said Mr Afenyo-Markin had categorically denied the allegations and insisted that he had confidence in the Minority Leader’s integrity. “The leader has denied it, and I know that it has never happened. This is not the kind of leader we have. We have a genuine-hearted leader. We have somebody who is blameless. We have somebody who is willing to fight for this country; he has never ever taken anything from anybody. He has never extorted Sammy Gyamfi,” he said. Defamation action Mr Darko said the Minority Leader was prepared to pursue legal remedies over the allegations, arguing that they had crossed the line from political disagreement into defamatory claims. “We are going to bring action against him. And you know, we’ll bring action against him for defamation,” he stated. His comments add another layer to the escalating exchanges between the GoldBod leadership and the Minority Caucus, particularly over questions surrounding the operations and financial transactions of the state-owned gold trading institution. The dispute has intensified as the Minority continues to demand greater scrutiny of GoldBod’s activities and the Bank of Ghana’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme, while the GoldBod leadership has defended its operations and challenged allegations made against it. ‘Much ado about nothing’ Mr Darko also dismissed the prospect of an investigation arising from the allegations, describing it as unlikely to yield anything substantive. “But as for this investigation, I don’t think that is going to go anywhere. It’s much ado about nothing,” he said. The latest development comes amid heightened political and public scrutiny of GoldBod and its role in Ghana’s gold trading regime, with the Minority insisting that questions surrounding transactions involving public funds must be subjected to proper parliamentary and institutional oversight. Mr Darko maintained that the allegations against Mr Afenyo-Markin would not distract the Minority from its broader oversight responsibilities.

items.title: Communal Clash: Otu threatens to revoke traditional rulers’ certificates of recognition
items.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR Cross River State Governor, Sen. Prince Bassey Edet Otu, has issued a stern warning to traditional rulers across the state, threatening to strip them of their certificates of recognition should peace collapse in their domains. The governor, represented by his Deputy, Hon Peter Odey, gave the warning on Monday at the 21st edition of the Leboku International New Yam Festival held at the Yakurr Peace Stadium, Ugep. The governor used the occasion to condemn the recent communal conflict between Ugep and Idomi communities in Yakurr Local Government Area, describing it as a “show of shame.” Otu disclosed that the government had contemplated cancelling this year’s Leboku festival in the wake of the crisis, but stepped back from the decision to avoid undermining the festival’s core mission of fostering peace, unity and brotherhood among the Yakurr people. “I wish to condemn in entirety the recent inter-communal war between Ugep and Idumi communities, which led to the loss of precious lives. “To the warring communities and other Yakurr communities which may have aligned with the combatants, I condemn this in its entirety. It was indeed a show of shame,” Otu said. The governor called on traditional institutions to shoulder greater responsibility for sustaining peace, particularly following the bloody Ugep-Idumi crisis. Turning directly to the Obol Lopon of Ugep and Paramount Ruler of Yakurr, Obol Ofem Ubana Eteng, Otu queried how the crisis was allowed to spiral despite the monarch’s traditional duty to safeguard peace. While commending Eteng’s 11-year reign as largely peaceful and impactful, the governor pressed him to tighten control over his subjects to forestall a repeat of the violence. “Your 11 years of reign on the throne of your forefathers have so far been peaceful and impactful. “What went wrong beyond your control this time? As the head of the entire Yakurr nation, you must control your subjects,” he said. Otu reminded village heads, clan heads, paramount rulers and other recognised traditional authorities that preserving peace, customs and tradition remained central to their roles and warned that defaulting monarchs would face sanctions. “The state government will therefore not fail to withdraw the certificate of recognition from any royal father where there is a breakdown of peace in his domain. Tourism cannot thrive in a volatile and chaotic environment,” the governor declared. He further announced that the state government would withhold recognition from either faction embroiled in the leadership tussle rocking Agoi Ibami, another Yakurr community. items.title: Oborevwori urges intelligence-led approach to tackle security challenges
items.description: Governor Sheriff Oborevwori of Delta has urged security agencies to adopt intelligence-led and preventive approaches to tackle Nigeria’s evolving security challenges. Oborevwori made the call on Monday in Asaba, when participants of the Advanced Intelligence Officers’ Course 16/2026, Defence Intelligence College, Karu, Abuja, paid him a courtesy visit. Represented by his Deputy, Mr Monday Onyeme, the governor said Nigeria needed to move decisively from reactive security management to preventive and intelligence-led governance. He said intelligence should not merely be gathered but translated into timely decisions, effective action and measurable security outcomes to strengthen national resilience and protect lives. “I urge you, as future senior intelligence and security leaders, to use the knowledge and experiences gained from this tour to strengthen national resilience and promote greater cooperation among security institutions,” he said. Oborevwori said contemporary security threats required collaborative engagement rather than isolated responses. The governor urged security agencies and stakeholders to sustain cooperation and provide operational support. He said Delta had demonstrated this approach through ‘Operation Delta Sweep’, established to strengthen joint security operations, reduce crime and protect lives and property across the state. The governor said regular State Security Council meetings also provided platforms for government and security agencies to assess emerging threats, share intelligence and coordinate appropriate responses. He said the state established the Office of the Special Adviser on Peace Building and Conflict Resolution to prevent conflicts, promote reconciliation and foster peaceful coexistence. According to him, the Office of the Special Adviser on Intelligence Gathering also strengthens grassroots intelligence and proactive crime prevention across communities in the state. “Delta recognises the importance of intelligence from the grassroots, which plays a vital role in providing early-warning information that supports timely security intervention,” he said. Oborevwori said the state recently convened a security summit themed: “Security: A Collective Responsibility”, bringing stakeholders together to unite against terrorism and other forms of criminality. He said the state was also developing a Data and Investment Intelligence Hub, following the 2026 State Economic and Investment Summit to support evidence-based decision-making. According to him, the hub will facilitate the collection, integration and analysis of reliable data for economic planning, investment promotion and security management. He said Delta also pursued regional security cooperation through platforms such as the Niger Delta Governors’ Forum to address cross-border threats affecting communities and critical assets. Oborevwori identified kidnapping, cultism, illegal bunkering and maritime insecurity among the threats requiring stronger regional cooperation and intelligence-sharing among neighbouring states and security agencies. Earlier, the Team Leader, Commodore Usman Bugaje, said Delta was selected for the study tour because of its strategic importance to Nigeria’s economy. Bugaje said participants considered the state’s oil and gas industry, offshore operations, transportation corridors, crude oil movement and other economic activities in determining the choice. “We also considered the various security agencies operating in the state,” he said, adding that participants were in Delta to examine its peculiar security challenges. He said the exercise aligned with the course theme, “Strengthening National Resilience Through Integrated Intelligence, Multi-Agency Coordination and Regional Security Cooperation.” Bugaje said the participants would interact with residents and stakeholders,vwhile appreciating the state government’s efforts to bring security agencies and traditional institutions together for peace. items.title: Opong-Fosu engages NDC Western region caucus ahead of formal declaration
items.description: As part of ongoing engagements with stakeholders of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) ahead of a formal declaration, former Minister for Local Government and Rural Development, Akwasi Opong-Fosu, has held discussions with the NDC Western Region Caucus. The engagement formed part of a broader process of listening, consultation and dialogue with key stakeholders across the party on its future, the consolidation of its values, and the important task of positioning the NDC for sustained political success beyond the current administration. At the heart of the engagement was a message of Restoration, Renewal and Resetting — restoring the values and principles that have sustained the NDC over the years, renewing the mindset and commitment of its members, and resetting the party’s structures and approach to respond effectively to the changing political and developmental aspirations of Ghanaians. Opong-Fosu emphasised the importance of consolidating the legacy of President John Dramani Mahama and ensuring that the gains of his administration provide a strong foundation for the future of both the party and the country. He noted that while delivering on the mandate entrusted to the NDC by the Ghanaian people remains paramount, the party must simultaneously begin the work of strengthening its internal cohesion, reconnecting with its grassroots, and preparing strategically for 2028 and beyond. The discussion also underscored the need to preserve the NDC as a broad-based, inclusive and values-driven political tradition in which every member — from the branch level to the national leadership — has a meaningful role to play. For Opong-Fosu, the next phase of the NDC’s development must be anchored in unity, discipline, institutional strength, and a renewed commitment to the founding ideals of probity, accountability and social justice. The engagement with the Western Region Caucus is part of a continuing stakeholder consultation process. Similar engagements are expected with various groups and constituencies within the party as Opong-Fosu continues to listen, consult and share his vision ahead of an appropriate time for a formal declaration. The central message remains clear: restore our values, renew our mindset, reset our party, consolidate the Mahama legacy, and build an NDC that is ready for 2028 and generations beyond.

items.title: Féguifoot : l’Assemblée générale extraordinaire et élective convoquée le 27 octobre 2026
items.description: La Fédération Guinéenne de Football (Féguifoot) s’apprête à franchir un cap décisif dans sa gouvernance. Dans un communiqué officiel signé par son Secrétaire Général, l’instance dirigeante du football national annonce la convocation de son Assemblée Générale Extraordinaire et Élective pour le mardi 27 octobre 2026 à Conakry, à partir de 10h00 GMT. Cette session s'inscrit dans le cadre de l'article 29.8 des Statuts de la Fédération. Elle intervient à la suite de la vacance de plus de 50 % des postes au sein du Comité Exécutif, déclenchant ainsi l'application de l'article 36.9 pour la réorganisation des instances dirigeantes. Un enjeu de gouvernance pour les quatre prochaines années L'ordre du jour de cette rencontre au sommet portera sur l'élection des nouveaux responsables de la Féguifoot pour un mandat de quatre (4) ans : Le Président de la Fédération ; Les Vice-Présidents ; Les membres du Comité Exécutif. Afin de garantir la régularité, la transparence et l'inclusivité du scrutin, l'ensemble des opérations électorales sera placé sous la supervision de la Commission Électorale de la Féguifoot, conformément à l'article 60.1 des Statuts. Les candidatures devront être soumises selon les modalités et délais réglementaires avant d'être examinées par les organes électoraux compétents. Présentée comme une étape cruciale pour la stabilité institutionnelle et la consolidation du football guinéen, cette Assemblée Générale sollicite la participation active de l'ensemble des membres statutaires et des acteurs du football national.

items.title: Kakum National Park killing: Brother recounts how resource guard was shot during patrol
items.description: The brother of a resource guard who was shot dead during a patrol at the Kakum National Park has recounted the moments leading to the fatal incident, saying the deceased called for help shortly after a gunshot was heard. The incident occurred during a routine patrol by wildlife officers, who were reportedly tracking suspected bushmeat hunters, locally referred to as “butchers”. The deceased, according to his brother Benjamin Ahadu, had worked as a resource guard at Kakum National Park for about 40 years. Mr Ahadu said the wildlife team began its routine patrol at about 10:00am on Friday when they identified an entry point allegedly used by suspected bushmeat hunters. He said the team subsequently heard gunshots and decided to monitor the movements of the suspected hunters in an attempt to apprehend them. According to him, the wildlife officers were not using torchlights, while the suspected hunters were using theirs, allowing the officers to track their movements in the darkness. Mr Ahadu said another gunshot was heard during the operation, initially leading the team to believe that one of their colleagues had fired a warning shot. He said the officers quickly moved towards the area and saw one of the suspects fleeing. While some members of the team pursued the fleeing suspect, Mr Ahadu said he remained with another suspected hunter. It was shortly afterwards that he heard his brother allegedly shout for help. “Ben, hurry, the guy has killed me.” Mr Ahadu said he could not immediately establish where the voice was coming from and called the other members of the team to help search for his brother. The team eventually found him dead, with what appeared to be a gunshot wound to his chest. The circumstances surrounding the shooting are subject to official investigations. Mr Ahadu also alleged that a similar incident occurred at the park about 11 years ago. He claimed the current shooting could be connected to that earlier incident, alleging that the brothers of a person who died during the previous event may have been involved in his brother’s death. That claim has not been independently established and would have to be tested through investigations. Mr Ahadu described his brother as a major source of support for their extended family. He said the deceased was the family’s breadwinner and had supported the education of about 15 people. He also paid tribute to his brother’s nearly four decades of service at Kakum National Park, describing him as someone who had dedicated his working life to protecting the park. The family is now calling for justice and says it will not resort to retaliation. “We can’t take the law into our hands, but we hope the law deals with them,” Mr Ahadu said. The death has renewed concerns about the risks faced by wildlife officers and resource guards who patrol protected areas and confront suspected illegal activities. The police and relevant wildlife authorities are expected to establish the circumstances surrounding the shooting and identify those responsible.

items.title: Burkina : Le Liptako va récolter 15 tonnes de poissons, une première pour cette région aride
items.description: BURKINA-LIPTAKO-PISCICULTURE-RECOLTE Burkina : Le Liptako va récolter 15 tonnes de poissons, une première pour cette région aride Dori, 24 août 2026 (AIB)-Grâce à l’implémentation des cages flottantes, la région aride du Liptako va récolter pour la première fois quinze tonnes de poissons au barrage de Yacouta, a appris l’AIB. Six mois après le lancement de l’empoissonnement des cages flottantes du barrage de Yacouta, l’heure de la moisson a débuté ce lundi, a annoncé le ministère en charge des Ressources halieutiques sur sa page Facebook. Au total, 18 cages flottantes doivent être récoltées, pour une production attendue de 15 tonnes de poissons, précise la même source. D’après le ministère, cette production locale devrait contribuer à renforcer la disponibilité du poisson dans la région, tout en créant des opportunités économiques pour les populations de Dori et des localités environnantes. Selon les initiateurs, l’expérience de Yacouta démontre la possibilité de développer une production halieutique locale en dépit des défis liés au contexte de la région. La production de poisson à Yacouta s’inscrit dans la dynamique de souveraineté alimentaire prônée par le président du Faso, Ibrahim Traoré, qui met l’accent sur la valorisation des ressources nationales et le développement de la production locale, conclut le ministère. items.title: Sowore, Amaechi trade words at NBA conference
items.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Presidential candidate Omoyele Sowore and former Rivers State governor Rotimi Amaechi, who represented former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, clashed on Monday during a political session at the 66th Annual General Conference of the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA) in Port Harcourt, Rivers State. The conference, themed “Beyond Limits,” brought together legal practitioners and political figures, with the political session focusing on Nigeria’s political future ahead of the 2027 general elections. At the event, there were discussions on the records of Nigerian politicians who have previously held public office and the impact of government policies, particularly fuel subsidy and transportation. Amaechi, responding to the arguments at the session, said Nigerians should not be deceived by politicians who had previously governed and failed to deliver. “I like what Amaechi said. He said that apart from Sowore and Adebayo, the rest of them have governed before and have failed. You guys should be apologising to the Nigerian people,” he said. Amaechi also argued that transportation policy should form part of the conversation around fuel subsidy, citing the railway project built by a former Rivers State governor. “We have a former governor of Rivers State who built a rail line that led to nowhere. If that rail line was well working, subsidy would have been working for Rivers State,” he said. He further criticised former Anambra State governor Peter Obi, saying he failed to adequately subsidise education during his tenure. “Peter Obi, for example, did not subsidise education in his state. Lecturers and doctors went on strike for 13 months. You can like him as a person, but he did not perform as a governor,” Amaechi said. The former governor also defended his record as Minister of Transportation, saying the Lagos-Ajaokuta railway was operational during his tenure. “In my time, Lagos-Ajaokuta railway was working. I do not know why it is not working under Tinubu. Same thing for Abuja-Kaduna rail,” he said. Amaechi subsequently directed his remarks at Sowore, urging lawyers from Rivers State to take the presidential candidate around the state. “Please, I need Rivers lawyers to take Sowore around. What is your experience?” he asked. He then told Sowore to remain silent while politicians with governing experience were speaking. “When politicians are talking, Sowore, close your mouth,” Amaechi said. The political session featured presidential candidates and representatives, including Sowore (presidential candidate of African Action Congress AAC), Peter Obi (presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress), Adewole Adebayo of the Social Democratic Party and Amaechi, who is the vice-presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress. items.title: Libération des mercenaires de Wagner au Mali : le clan Haftar, nouvel interlocuteur privilégié du FLA
items.description: Saddam Haftar, le fils du maître de l’est libyen, a orchestré le transfert jusqu’à Benghazi des deux ex-mercenaires de Wagner, libérés le 20 août par le Front de libération de l’Azawad (FLA). Voici ce que l’on sait du dessous de ces négociations.

items.title: Le CJN remporte la 2e édition du maracana de Tita
items.description: BURKINA-SANGUIE-POUNI-MARACANA-DREAM'S-MULTI-SERVICE-FINALE Le CJN remporte la 2e édition du maracana de Tita Tita, 24 août 2026 (AIB) – Le Club des jeunes de Naab-ziniguin (CJN) a remporté le dimanche 23 août, la 2e édition du tournoi maracana Dream’s Multi service de Tita en battant en finale, Zongo Hamado Athlétique (ZH9) sur le terrain de l’unité, par le score de 2 buts à 1. Placée sous le signe de la cohésion sociale et de la paix par le sport, cette apothéose a tenu toutes ses promesses. Dominateurs dès la première période, les « rouges » de CJN ont regagné les vestiaires avec un avantage d'un but à zéro (1-0). De retour des vestiaires, les « verts » de ZH9 Athlétique ont intensifié la pression, parvenant à recoller au score. Cependant, un sursaut d'orgueil et un ultime break des joueurs de CJN ont scellé le sort de la rencontre. Score final : 2 buts à 1 en faveur de CJN. À l'issue du match, les équipes et les meilleurs acteurs de la compétition ont été récompensés à la hauteur de leurs efforts. L'équipe championne, la CJN, gagne le trophée, un jeu de maillots, 2 ballons, des médailles et une enveloppe financière de 200 000 F CFA. ZH9 Athlétique qui occupe la 2e place bénéficie d'un jeu de maillots, 1 ballon, des médailles et 150 000 F CFA. Les équipes classées 3e et 4e ont eu droit à des dotations composées de ballons et d'enveloppes de 75 000 F CFA et 50 000 F CFA. Des prix individuels, il y en a eu. Le meilleur gardien, Amado Yogo a reçu une médaille et 10 000 F CFA, le meilleur buteur, Félix Nebié gagne une médaille et 10 000 F CFA pendant que le meilleur supporter, Amado Sawadogo est reparti avec 5 000 F CFA. La cérémonie a enregistré la présence de plusieurs personnalités, notamment le représentant de la marraine Nadine Tiemounou/Badiel (PDS de Pouni), le parrain Kassoum Kaboré (PDG de Boudnoma Trading), ainsi que le coparrain Mahama Nebié. Dans leurs interventions, les autorités coutumières, administratives et le promoteur du tournoi, Abdoul Kader Simporé (PDG de Dream's Multi Services), ont salué la mobilisation et l'esprit de fair-play qui ont prévalu tout au long de l'épreuve. Tous ont magnifié le sport comme un puissant vecteur de rassemblement et de paix. Des intermèdes musicaux ont agrémenté cette journée festive, dont les rideaux sont tombés sur une note de satisfaction générale et une promesse de rendez-vous prise pour la 3e édition en 2027. Agence d'information du Burkina JS/PB

items.title: Qui est Saâd Arous, le nouveau président de l’Anie ?
items.description: Changement à la tête de l’Autorité nationale indépendante des élections ( Anie ). Le président de la République, Abdelmadjid Tebboune, a mis fin aux fonctions de Karim Khalfane qui occupait le poste de président de l’Autorité par intérim depuis la démission de Mohamed Charfi le 27 novembre 2025. « Le président de la République, M. Abdelmadjid Tebboune, a signé, ce jour, deux décrets présidentiels, mettant fin, en vertu du premier, aux fonctions de M. Karim Khelfane en qualité de président par intérim de l'Autorité nationale indépendante des élections, et nommant, par le second, M. Saâd Arous à la présidence de l'Autorité nationale indépendante des élections », a indiqué la Présidence de la République ce lundi 24 août. La fin de mission de M. Khalfane survient moins de deux mois après la tenue des élections législatives du 2 juillet dernier qu’il a supervisées. Saâd Arous, un avocat à la tête de l’Autorité nationale indépendante des élections M. Arous, qui doit préparer les prochaines élections communales, occupait jusque-là le poste de président du groupe parlementaire du tiers présidentiel au Conseil de la nation (Sénat) et faisait partie du Comité exécutif de l’Union parlementaire arabe. Avocat près la Cour suprême et le Conseil d’État, M. Arous avait été nommé par le président de la République, Abdelmadjid Tebboune, sénateur du tiers présidentiel en juin 2020. En tant que président du groupe parlementaire du tiers présidentiel au Conseil de la nation, Saâd Arous a effectué plusieurs déplacements à l’étranger où il a représenté la chambre haute du Parlement algérien, notamment aux travaux de la 39ᵉ session du Comité exécutif de l’Union parlementaire arabe, où il a mis en garde contre l’expansionnisme israélien. « Le projet colonial expansionniste sioniste ne vise pas seulement le peuple palestinien, mais menace également des terres arabes et cherche à soumettre le présent et l’avenir de la Nation à un imaginaire sioniste maladif », a-t-il déclaré. En novembre 2020, lors du débat sur le projet de loi relatif à la lutte contre les crimes d’enlèvement, il a appelé, dans un entretien à La Patrie News, la société civile à « apporter sa contribution dans la lutte contre le phénomène d’enlèvement d’enfants en Algérie ». L’article Qui est Saâd Arous, le nouveau président de l’Anie ? est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Logements sociaux pour les fonctionnaires : le Gouvernement lance une plateforme d’inscription et appelle à la vigilance
items.description: Le Gouvernement guinéen s’apprête à lancer un projet de logements sociaux destiné aux fonctionnaires de l’État. L’annonce a été faite par le ministère de la Modernisation de l’Administration et de la Fonction publique, dirigé par Faya François Bourouno, à travers un communiqué rendu public ce lundi 24 août 2026. Cette initiative s’inscrit dans la volonté des autorités d’améliorer durablement les conditions de vie et de travail des agents de l’État, en leur facilitant l’accès à des logements « décents, modernes et accessibles ». Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de ce programme, une plateforme numérique officielle a été mise à la disposition des fonctionnaires. Celle-ci doit notamment permettre aux agents de participer au sondage d’appétence et de prendre connaissance des conditions ainsi que des critères d’éligibilité au projet. Les fonctionnaires sont invités à effectuer leur démarche exclusivement via la plateforme officielle : https://logementfonctionnaire.cloud/ Le département de Faya François Bourouno précise que les agents devront suivre attentivement les communications officielles concernant les modalités d’accès à la plateforme, les conditions et délais d’inscription, ainsi que le processus de sélection et d’attribution des logements. Le Gouvernement met en garde contre les démarches frauduleuses Face aux risques d’arnaques ou de fausses inscriptions, le ministère appelle les fonctionnaires à la plus grande vigilance. Il rappelle que toute procédure liée au programme devra obligatoirement passer par le dispositif officiellement mis en place par le Gouvernement. « Aucune inscription, perception de frais ou intervention effectuée en dehors du dispositif officiellement annoncé ne saurait engager la responsabilité du Gouvernement », prévient le communiqué. Ci-dessus Communiqué L’article Logements sociaux pour les fonctionnaires : le Gouvernement lance une plateforme d’inscription et appelle à la vigilance est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: 2027: Obi disagrees with Atiku on subsidy, faults mismanagement of proceeds
items.description: By Bayo Wahab The Presidential candidate of the Nigerian Democratic Party, Peter Obi, has disagreed with the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, over his proposed return of fuel subsidy if elected in 2027. Obi also accused the federal government of mismanaging the savings from the proceeds of fuel susidy removal. The ex-governor of Anambra State spoke on Monday at the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA) conference in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, while reacting to the debate over whether fuel subsidy should be restored as proposed by Atiku. Atiku, who campaigned for the removal of fuel subsidy during the 2023 presidential election, has said he would restore the policy if elected president in 2027. But Obi maintained that subsidy removal remained necessary, arguing that the problem was the failure to properly manage and invest the resources saved from the policy. “I subscribe and I maintain that we need to remove subsidy. Mismanagement of the proceeds should not be the reason for not removing it,” Obi said. He argued that the government should have provided alternatives to cushion the impact of subsidy removal on Nigerians while ensuring that the savings were deployed to productive sectors. “What we should have done is that when we removed it, we should have given the people alternative usage for the subsidy,” he said. According to Obi, the resources recovered from subsidy removal have not been adequately managed, alleging that they were also being “mismanaged and stolen.” “What we have today is that that removal and the attendant resources being recovered is also being mismanaged and stolen,” he said. The former governor said he had anticipated the need for a structured approach to subsidy removal and had outlined his position in his manifesto ahead of the 2023 election. “Go to my manifesto, I said it before, I said I will do it in an organised manner and whatever we recover would be invested appropriately,” Obi said. President Bola Tinubu announced the removal of the petrol subsidy on his inauguration day in May 2023, triggering a sharp increase in petrol prices and widespread concerns over the rising cost of living. While the policy has been defended by the Federal Government as necessary to reduce fiscal pressure and redirect public resources, opposition figures have continued to criticise its implementation and the use of the resulting savings. The post 2027: Obi disagrees with Atiku on subsidy, faults mismanagement of proceeds appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Mahama officially nominates James Agalga as Acting Majority Leader
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has officially nominated the Member of Parliament for Builsa North, James Agalga, to serve as Acting Majority Leader of Parliament. The nomination was communicated to the House during the emergency sitting of Parliament on Monday, August 24, following the recall of Parliament at the behest of the President. Speaker of Parliament Alban Bagbin read the President’s letter conveying the nomination to Members of Parliament. The development comes as Parliament begins a five-day emergency sitting to consider urgent business outlined by the President. The sitting, which runs from Monday, August 24 to Friday, August 28, is also expected to consider the nominations of three persons to the Supreme Court, two ministerial nominees and the Banks and Specialised Deposit-Taking Institutions Amendment Bill. Speaker Bagbin has directed the House to restrict its business to the matters for which it was recalled and indicated that no other business would be admitted during the emergency session.

items.title: DSS probes NFF
items.description: BY TONY UBANI The Department of State Services, DSS, has joined other security operatives in investigating the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) into the utilisation of the N17bn Federal Government intervention fund released to the Nigeria Football Federation for players’ wages and bonuses. The fund was approved by President Bola Tinubu in 2024 to clear outstanding payments owed to Nigeria’s national teams. An authoritative source informed Vanguard yesterday that the DSS has beamed their searchlight on officials of the Nigeria Football Federation to show proof on what they did with the massive fund released to the Glass house. ‘’It’s a normal thing for DSS to go through all documents relating to the funds released them’’, our source said dismissing fears of witch hunt or hounding. The latest probe comes amid persistent public concerns over the administration of Nigerian football teams that have suffered severe systemic decline, highlighted by the Super Eagles missing consecutive FIFA World Cups and the historic failure of the Super Falcons to qualify for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil. The Super Falcons lost 1-0 to Cameroon in the 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) quarter-finals, which ended their title defense and missed automatic World Cup qualification, subsequently facing a playoff path involving South Africa. The Banyana Banyana defeated Nigeria’s Super Falcons 2–1 in the Women’s World Cup qualification playoff. Nigeria has played in every single FIFA Women’s World Cup since the tournament began in 1991, making this the first time they failed to qualify. The executive committee of the NFF headed by Ibrahim Gusau is under intense pressure to resign following the spate of failures and also following the resignation of more than half of its members. Eight of the 13 members of the NFF board have allegedly quit their positions and this development could halt the scheduled September 27 elections into the board of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) slated for Lafia, Nasarawa. The post DSS probes NFF appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nigerian NHS worker faces ban after driving against traffic in UK
items.description: A Nigerian NHS worker in Manchester, United Kingdom, Innocent Ayodele could lose his driving license after he was caught driving the wrong way on a motorway slip road while trying to avoid a traffic jam. Ayodele was stopped after driving against the flow of traffic on an entry slip road to the M61. He reportedly told police that he was trying to get home to his pregnant wife after finishing work. However, a police officer who confronted him said the manoeuvre was dangerous, noting that Ayodele could have collided with another vehicle. The incident was brought before Preston Magistrates’ Court, where Ayodele apologised for his actions. He already has nine penalty points on his driving licence and could face a driving ban when he is sentenced at a later date. The case comes amid concerns over the dangers posed by motorists who drive in the wrong direction on motorways. Figures obtained by the Press Association showed that 31 drivers were charged in England and Wales over a 30-week period for offences involving driving the wrong way on motorways. National Highways data also recorded 947 reports involving “oncoming vehicles” on England’s motorways in the 12 months to May 11, although the agency said the figure could include unconfirmed reports. The agency stressed that confirmed cases of wrong-way driving remain rare but said every report is treated seriously. Motoring safety experts have warned that driving against traffic on a motorway can result in potentially fatal head-on collisions.
