items.title: Afenyo-Markin may struggle to wriggle out of GoldBod loss claims – Edem Senanu
items.description: Anti-corruption campaigner Edem Senanu believes Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin may face difficulties explaining his recent claims that the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) incurred losses under the Bank of Ghana’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme. According to Mr Senanu, a review of the 182-page International Monetary Fund (IMF) report cited in the debate does not support the Minority Leader’s claim that GoldBod recorded a loss. “I took a look at the 182-page IMF report, and Joy, you had done a good job of fact-checking. There were 47 mentions of the GoldBod, not once mentioned that there was a loss,” he said on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Monday, August 24. “Indeed, the Bank of Ghana had made a loss there, and essentially owns the GoldBod. So I was wondering why the Minority Leader would come and lead that kind of allegation,” he added. He added that the coming days and weeks would reveal how the Minority Leader and the Minority in Parliament respond to the questions surrounding the claim. “I’m not quite sure how they’re going to wriggle out of this one,” Mr Senanu said. He also questioned whether adequate checks were conducted before the allegation was made, suggesting that Afenyo-Markin could now be faced with the task of managing the fallout from the claim. “I’m wondering whether the people behind the scenes did not do a good job of checking what they were saying. And potentially he may have been set up for a situation where now they have to manage what they do next,” Mr Senanu said. His comments come amid a growing political debate over the financial performance of GoldBod and the interpretation of the IMF’s latest assessment of Ghana’s economic programme. Mr Senanu also observed that Afenyo-Markin had appeared more measured in his recent public engagements, describing the Minority Leader’s calmer approach as useful in managing the controversy. “It’s good that he’s sober, because if you look at the data, it doesn’t support what he said,” he noted.

items.title: GES opens WAEC portal for 2026 school placement data submission
items.description: The Ghana Education Service (GES) has announced that the West African Examinations Council (WAEC) portal for the online capturing and uploading of candidates’ school selection data for the 2026 placement exercise will open from Monday, August 24 to Thursday, August 27, 2026. According to a press statement issued on Monday, August 24, the directive affects all Heads of Junior High Schools (JHSs) and forms part of preparations for the placement of candidates into senior high schools and technical and vocational education and training institutions following the 2026 Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE). In a directive to Heads of JHSs, the GES Management said the WAEC portal would be available during the four-day period to enable schools to capture and submit candidates’ school selection information. The GES has also directed headteachers who have not yet completed the uploading of candidates’ school choices on the Computerised School Selection and Placement System (CSSPS) portal for pre-testing to do so by the close of work on Monday, August 24. After completing the CSSPS pre-testing upload, the headteachers are expected to proceed to the WAEC portal to capture and upload the required school selection data. The Service has therefore urged schools to adhere strictly to the respective deadlines to prevent delays in the processing of candidates’ information. The exercise requires schools to ensure that candidates’ school choices are accurately captured before the information is submitted through the designated system. The GES said the WAEC portal has been configured to allow the same school ID and password to be used simultaneously on multiple computers. According to the Service, the arrangement is intended to assist schools with large numbers of candidates to undertake the data-capturing exercise concurrently. The facility is expected to make the process faster and more efficient by allowing several officials or computers to work on the data at the same time. GES said this would help schools complete the exercise within the stipulated period and facilitate the timely submission of candidates’ information. The Service has directed Metro, Municipal and District Directors of Education, together with Examination Coordinators, to closely supervise and monitor the exercise. They have been tasked with ensuring that the data of all eligible candidates are properly captured, verified and submitted within the specified timeframe. The directive places responsibility on education authorities at the local level to monitor schools under their jurisdiction and address any challenges that may arise during the exercise. The supervision is also intended to minimise errors and ensure that information submitted for the placement exercise accurately reflects the school choices of eligible candidates. Regional Directors of Education have also been asked to communicate the directive to all relevant schools and education officials within their respective jurisdictions. The directive follows an earlier GES letter, referenced GES/HO/DG/494/2026 and dated August 18, 2026, concerning the school selection and placement exercise. The latest instruction is aimed at ensuring that all administrative and data-capturing processes are completed on time to support the 2026 placement exercise. With the WAEC portal available only until Thursday, August 27, schools have been urged to begin or complete the required processes without delay. Headteachers who are yet to complete the CSSPS pre-testing upload have been given the earlier deadline of close of work on August 24, after which they are expected to proceed with the WAEC portal submission. GES has stressed the importance of accurate data capture, verification and timely submission, given the potential impact of errors or omissions on candidates’ placement arrangements. The GES is urging all concerned officials to comply fully with the instructions and make effective use of the available period to complete the process for all eligible candidates.

items.title: Family, legal team of Imaan and Hadi voice concerns over medical facilities at Adiala jail
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The families and legal team of incarcerated lawyers and human rights activists Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Ali Chatta have voiced concerns over the medical facilities available at Adiala jail. On January 24, rights lawyers Imaan and Hadi were sentenced by an Islamabad sessions court to a total of 17 years in jail on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca). Following their convictions, which were widely condemned by lawyers and United Nations (UN) experts , the couple challenged their convictions before the Islamabad High Court (IHC) on February 7. In a statement issued on Monday, the family and legal team said they were satisfied with the weekly meetings with the couple at the jail. However, they said Imaan had been experiencing health issues for the past three weeks, raising concerns about the medical facilities available at the jail. “Imaan had initially complained of heavy bleeding from her gums, but there was no dentist available to examine her at the jail. We arranged for medicine to be sent to her after consulting our dentist, but not all of it reached her,” the statement alleged. The following week, Imaan also suffered from stomach problems, and medical attention remained inadequate, it added. “Worse, a medicine, Zedron, meant primarily for cancer patients and which specifically states that it should not be given to women of childbearing age, was administered to her to stop her nausea and vomiting,” the statement claimed. For the past week, the family and legal team said Imaan had been suffering from a serious chest infection. “They conducted a blood test which showed a high white blood cell count, indicating an infection. She needs to undergo a chest X-ray, but the jail authorities have still not arranged one to determine the cause of the infection and rule out serious diseases such as tuberculosis,” they said. They maintained that their concern was compounded by the alarming fact that inmates in the women’s section of Adiala jail who had been diagnosed with infectious diseases were not isolated but housed alongside other inmates, as well as children. “The women’s medical facilities and the availability of doctors leave a lot to be desired,” they stated. “This is a health crisis in the jail, and the well-being of prisoners is the responsibility of the state, which must not take it lightly,” the statement said. They reiterated that all these health issues could be avoided if their applications for suspension of sentence were heard in a timely manner. They urged the jail authorities and the government to arrange Imaan’s chest X-ray as soon as possible and provide adequate medical facilities, including dental care, to all women prisoners. They emphasised that detainees with infectious diseases should be isolated or quarantined with dignity to protect other detainees; that specialist doctors and access to relevant medication should be provided to all detainees; and that the government should not oppose the applications for suspension of sentence filed by Imaan and Hadi, which are scheduled to be heard by the IHC on Sept 8, 2026.

items.title: Jeux mondiaux des robots humanoïdes 2026 : un laboratoire de performance des êtres en carbone
items.description: Beijing, la capitale chinoise, accueille du 22 au 26 août 2026, la 2e édition des Jeux mondiaux des robots humanoïdes. La cérémonie d'ouverture de l'événement, intervenue dans la soirée du 22 août, dans l'enceinte de l'Anneau national de patinage de vitesse, a donné un aperçu des compétitions. Dans un décor de film de science-fiction, des robots humanoïdes bien entraînés, ont proposé un spectacle haut en couleur au public. Plus de 2 056 robots humanoïdes de 666 équipes issus de 16 pays s'affrontent dans plusieurs disciplines sportives comme le tennis de table, la boxe, des courses, le football, le saut à la corde ou encore le soulevé de poids… Cette compétition illustre la fulgurance dans le développement du secteur de la robotique ces dernières années en Chine. De simples spécimens de robots qui servaient à des essais, l'on est passé à une étape de la robotique industrielle qui se déploie dans plusieurs secteurs d'activités avec des performances qui défient l'imagination. Désormais, en Chine, les robots humanoïdes prennent exclusivement en charge certains travaux. De la cuisine au service de nettoyage en passant par la livraison, il n'est de secret pour ces êtres en carbone. Les Jeux mondiaux des robots humanoïdes qui réunissent des entreprises chinoises et du monde entier sont le symbole que ces inventions peuvent embrasser tous les domaines de l'activité humaine. Ils sont aussi la traduction parfaite des initiatives innovantes dans le secteur. En accueillant les Jeux mondiaux des robots humanoïdes, la Chine confirme son statut de leader en matière d'innovation et d'inventivité dans le secteur. Un rapport sectoriel publié récemment lors de la Conférence mondiale sur la robotique 2026, indique que la Chine a livré plus de 40 000 robots humanoïdes au premier semestre de cette année, portant sa part des livraisons mondiales à 97 %. Les applications concrètes dont font preuve les robots humanoïdes chinois dans divers secteurs d'activités prouvent une fois de plus que l'expertise des entreprises du pays est solide et convaincante. La tenue des Jeux mondiaux des robots humanoïdes à Beijing confirme également l'émergence d'un écosystème « quatre-en-un » articulé autour de la normalisation, de la formation des talents, de la coopération internationale et des infrastructures d'innovation. L'organisation d'une telle compétition nécessite la disponibilité d'infrastructures appropriées et de ressources humaines qualifiées et une volonté de toujours aller de l'avant. Les Jeux mondiaux des robots humanoïdes se présentent pour la Chine comme un laboratoire d'expériences des différents spécimens créés par les entreprises. À titre illustratif, un robot humanoïde chinois a établi un nouveau record du 100 mètres avec 9,39 secondes, pulvérisant celui de l'athlète jamaïcain Usain Bolt, qui était de 9,58 secondes. C'est la preuve que l'innovation technologique chinoise innerve à un rythme flamboyant le secteur de la robotique. Plus qu'un divertissement, les Jeux mondiaux des robots humanoïdes dessinent les contours d'un avenir où les humains et les robots humanoïdes devront cohabiter et apprendre à travailler ensemble. Au-delà de la compétition, l'événement, organisé par le gouvernement municipal de Beijing, China Media Group (CMG), l'Organisation mondiale de coopération sur la robotique (WRCO), et le Conseil international de la RoboCup Asie-Pacifique (RCAP), met en avant les échanges technologiques et offre une plate-forme mondiale de partage d'expériences dans le secteur de la robotique. Karim BADOLO CGTN Français

items.title: Mangu attacks- death toll hits 28, MDA demands sustained military action
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – The Mwaghavul Development Association, MDA, has condemned the recent attacks on communities in Mwaghavul land, saying 28 people were killed in separate attacks on Bin Mper and Murish communities in Mangu Local Government Area of Plateau State. The association also called on the Federal, Plateau State and local governments to prioritise the protection of lives and property, stressing the need for sustained and decisive military operations to end attacks on vulnerable communities. The MDA made the call in a statement signed by its Director of Public Affairs, Friday Derwam, after an extraordinary meeting of its Central Working Committee, CWC, at the weekend and made available to journalists in Jos on Monday. The meeting, according to the association, reviewed reports from its National Executive Committee, internal constitutional matters and the impact of government policies on the Mwaghavul people, with particular attention to the worsening security situation in their ancestral communities. The association described the attacks as “unprovoked acts of aggression” by armed bandits, saying 28 lives were lost in Bin Mper and Murish, while homes, farmlands and other property worth millions of naira were destroyed. “MDA mourns this devastating loss and stands in complete solidarity with the affected families,” the statement said. While condemning the attacks, the association commended the security agencies for their proactive measures and rapid intervention, which it said helped to prevent further escalation of the situation. It specifically commended the General Officer Commanding, GOC, 3 Division, Nigerian Army, General Maxwell Dangana who is also the Commander of Operation Enduring Peace, OPEP, for what it described as a swift operational response and improved inter-agency collaboration in the affected communities. The MDA also praised Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, for his response to the attacks, particularly his visit to Bin Mper community. It said the governor’s visit, deployment of additional security personnel, pledge of relief assistance and commitment to constructing access roads to improve security response had offered some reassurance to residents. The association equally commended Mwaghavul youths for their resilience, courage and vigilance in protecting their communities, but urged them to operate within the confines of the law. “The CWC assures our brave youth of the Association’s unwavering support, ongoing prayers and continuous backing as they stand firm in safeguarding our communities,” it stated. On the wider security situation, the MDA maintained that protecting lives and property remained the primary responsibility of government at all levels. It therefore called for sustained military operations to secure vulnerable communities, dismantle bandit hideouts and end the cycle of violence across Plateau State and other parts of the country. The association further urged the Federal, state and local governments to place national security above political and economic considerations, insisting that the safety of citizens must remain a priority. According to the MDA, residents would only be able to return to their farms and rebuild their homes and livelihoods when communities are adequately secured and the persistent attacks brought to an end. items.title: Soudan du Sud: les élections pourraient accroître le risque de crimes atroces, alertent des enquêteurs de l’ONU
items.description: Les premières élections nationales au Soudan du Sud depuis l’indépendance, en 2011, pourraient alimenter de nouvelles violences plutôt que contribuer à sortir le pays du conflit, ont averti jeudi des enquêteurs indépendants de l’ONU, qui redoutent, en l’absence de dialogue politique et de garanties pour un scrutin crédible, un risque accru de « crimes atroces ». Dans son nouveau rapport, la Commission des Nations Unies sur les droits de l'homme au Soudan du Sud constate que « de multiples facteurs de risque de crimes atroces convergent », notamment la reprise du conflit armé dans plusieurs régions du pays, l’abandon d’une politique inclusive à Juba, ainsi que l’affaiblissement de l’espace civique et des garanties constitutionnelles. Selon cette commission mandatée par le Conseil des droits de l’homme des Nations Unies, des pans importants de la population restent exclus d’une participation politique significative. « Sans un retour à un dialogue authentique et inclusif, la lutte politique autour des élections risque d’aggraver les divisions existantes plutôt que d’offrir un moyen pacifique de les résoudre », alertent les enquêteurs onusiens. « Les Sud-Soudanais méritent une élection qui leur donne la parole, et non une élection qui mette leur vie en danger », a déclaré Yasmin Sooka, présidente de la Commission. Les risques d’une nouvelle flambée de violences « Une démocratie pacifique ne peut se construire sur les fondements du conflit armé, de la peur et de l’exclusion. Or, les garanties mêmes destinées à empêcher un retour à la guerre sont en train d’être démantelées alors que le pays se dirige vers les urnes. » Au-delà des postures politiques, la Commission alerte sur une accumulation de facteurs susceptibles de faire dérailler le processus électoral et de raviver les violences. Selon le cadre d’analyse des crimes atroces de l’ONU, ces facteurs de risque se renforcent mutuellement. Reprise du conflit, affaiblissement des institutions, impunité, gouvernance exclusive, corruption, recul de l’espace civique et discours incendiaires se conjuguent, tandis que les garde-fous – surveillance du cessez-le-feu, justice indépendante et dialogue politique inclusif – ont été affaiblis ou suspendus. Dans ces conditions, la Commission note qu’il ne faut pas laisser les élections se transformer en un « nouveau théâtre de violences ». Alors que les armes refont leur apparition, les garanties d’une compétition politique pacifique disparaissent. « Il s’agit là d’une trajectoire extrêmement dangereuse. Le Soudan du Sud ne peut pas construire un avenir démocratique en excluant ceux avec lesquels il est en désaccord. Les parties doivent renouer un véritable dialogue, rétablir le consensus et créer les conditions permettant une compétition politique sans exclusion ni violence », a insisté Barney Afako, expert de la Commission. Conditions indispensables pour un scrutin crédible et pacifique La Commission énumère plusieurs conditions indispensables à un scrutin crédible et pacifique : une cessation effective et contrôlée des hostilités, des forces de sécurité nationales unifiées sous un commandement non partisan, des institutions électorales indépendantes et un mécanisme impartial de règlement des litiges. Les enquêteurs demandent également des mesures contre les discours de haine et l’incitation à la violence, ainsi qu’une participation politique équitable de l’ensemble des partis. Dans cet avis, la Commission appelle le gouvernement et les signataires de l’Accord de paix régional à mettre fin aux hostilités et à relancer sans délai un dialogue inclusif associant notamment la faction Mouvement populaire de libération du Soudan en opposition (SPLM-IO) de Riek Machar, les groupes dissidents, la société civile, les femmes et les jeunes. Elle réclame aussi la libération des opposants détenus, dont Riek Machar, à moins qu’ils soient rapidement jugés par une juridiction indépendante et impartiale, dans le respect des normes internationales. La Commission exhorte enfin l’Union africaine, l’Autorité intergouvernementale pour le développement (IGAD), l’ONU et les partenaires internationaux à renforcer leur diplomatie préventive. items.title: Samuel Eto’o vole au secours de Gianni Infantino
items.description: Samuel Eto’o a apporté son soutien à Gianni Infantino, dont la gouvernance de la FIFA est de plus en plus contestée à quelques mois de l’élection présidentielle prévue en mars 2027. Dans un entretien accordé à CNN, le président de la Fédération camerounaise de football a estimé que le patron de la FIFA n’avait « rien fait de mal », prenant notamment sa défense après l’abandon de son projet controversé visant à ouvrir davantage le football aux investisseurs privés. L’ancien attaquant du FC Barcelone et de l’Inter Milan a surtout mis en avant l’impact de la présidence d’Infantino sur le football africain. « Il a aidé notre continent. Il a aidé nos fédérations à se développer beaucoup plus rapidement, et nous devons le reconnaître » , a déclaré Eto’o, appelant à soutenir le dirigeant suisse pour son bilan. L’ancien international camerounais est même allé plus loin en affirmant : « Le président Gianni Infantino a changé le football. » Selon Eto’o, l’élargissement de la Coupe du monde a notamment permis à plusieurs nations de bénéficier d’opportunités qui leur étaient auparavant difficilement accessibles. Le président de la Fédération camerounaise a également défendu Infantino face aux critiques suscitées par son projet d’ouverture aux investisseurs privés, finalement abandonné. « Je ne pense pas que le président ait fait quoi que ce soit de mal » , a-t-il affirmé, estimant que les tensions actuelles sont notamment liées aux prochaines élections à la FIFA. Eto’o a même suggéré que ce projet pourrait être remis sur la table si Infantino était réélu en mars 2027. Alors que l’UEFA, la Confédération asiatique (AFC) et la Concacaf ont exprimé leur opposition au dirigeant suisse, la Confédération africaine de football (CAF) lui a, de son côté, renouvelé son soutien. Samuel Eto’o a également évoqué les bénéfices que pourrait apporter une redistribution plus importante des ressources vers les fédérations africaines. Selon lui, un tel système permettrait notamment au Cameroun d’attirer davantage de grands talents. « Nous voulons voir des Messi, des Mbappé, mais j’aimerais voir Mbappé jouer pour le Cameroun » , a lancé Eto’o, faisant référence aux origines camerounaises du père de l’attaquant français. Un soutien appuyé à Gianni Infantino, alors que le président de la FIFA se retrouve au centre d'une bataille politique à l'approche de l'élection de 2027. items.title: Médina Baye : la Police déploie un dispositif de 48 heures pour la confection de passeports
items.description: La direction de la Police des étrangers et des titres de voyage (DPETV), en collaboration avec l’organisation islamique sénégalaise, Jamiyatu Ansaarud Din, a mis en place un ”dispositif exceptionnel” de deux jours pour la confection de passeports à Médina Baye (Kaolack, centre), à l’occasion du Gamou international, ”afin de rapprocher le service des nombreux pèlerins présents dans la cité religieuse”, a constaté l’APS. Cette opération obéit aux instructions de la hiérarchie, notamment du directeur général de la Police nationale, Mame Seydou Ndour, en coordination avec la DPETV, a fait savoir l’adjudant de police Mansour Faye, chef du centre des passeports de Kaolack. ”C’est un dispositif exceptionnel que nous avons mis en place sur instruction de la hiérarchie, comme cela a été fait lors d’autres grands événements religieux”, a-t-il dit, précisant que le dispositif est prévu pour une durée de 48 heures. Il a précisé que les usagers peuvent se présenter directement au centre délocalisé de Médina Baye, sans rendez-vous, pour leur enrôlement et l’accomplissement des formalités nécessaires à l’établissement de leur passeport. La mesure est favorablement accueillie par les pèlerins, à l’image de Pape Mayip Gueye et Adama Minthé, qui saluent cette initiative favorisant le rapprochement des services de l’administration des usagers. items.title: Education Minister inducts KNUST Vice Chancellor as Chair of Technology and Consultancy Centre
items.description: The Minister for Education, Haruna Iddrisu, has inducted the newly appointed Vice Chancellor of the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Prof. Christian Agyare, as Chair of the University’s Technology and Consultancy Centre. The induction took place during a courtesy call by Prof. Agyare on the Education Minister in Accra, where they discussed key priorities for the development of the university. The discussions focused on science and technology education, research, student accommodation and infrastructure development. Mr Iddrisu congratulated Prof. Agyare on his appointment and assured him of government’s support as he begins his tenure. He said government, through the Ghana Education Trust Fund (GETFund), would support the completion of the KNUST Teaching Hospital. According to the Minister, the facility would strengthen teaching and learning, particularly in health-related disciplines, while also providing healthcare services to residents in surrounding communities. Mr Iddrisu further urged KNUST to place greater emphasis on Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) education to produce more graduates with skills relevant to the changing demands of the Ghanaian economy. He also called on the new Vice Chancellor to strengthen collaboration with private hostel operators to help provide affordable accommodation for students. In response, Prof. Agyare assured the Ministry of his commitment to advancing KNUST’s mandate and working closely with government and other stakeholders. He said the university was already taking steps to strengthen its focus on science by directing more resources towards the re-equipping and retooling of laboratories. Prof. Agyare added that KNUST was strengthening its academic programmes and research in Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), Artificial Intelligence (AI), emerging technologies and other areas considered critical to the needs of the new generation. On student accommodation, he said the university was engaging private hostel owners to explore ways of making accommodation more affordable for students. Prof. Agyare further pledged to deepen stakeholder engagement during his tenure, stressing that collaboration would be essential to advancing the university’s academic, research and development objectives.

items.title: The Atlantic announces Jessica Goldstein as SVP of events
items.description: The Atlantic has hired Jessica Goldstein as senior vice president of events, who will work in partnership with managing director for events Evan Smith to lead and produce the magazine’s robust live programs nationwide. She begins with The Atlantic in early September. Jessica has spent her career telling stories through reporting and creating live experiences that resonate far beyond the stage. She spent eight years creating and leading NPR’s live cultural programming, including creating the Tiny Desk Contest, NPR’s annual search for new musical talent, and the How I Built This Summit. She most recently led the Skoll Foundation’s global convenings strategy and directed the Skoll World Forum. At The Atlantic , she will work with Evan to lead one of the most influential and long-running events practices in media. The Atlantic convenes dozens of annual in-person and virtual events that reach thousands of people every year, anchored by its flagship event, The Atlantic Festival , which returns to New York City September 17–19, after being held for nearly two decades in Washington, D.C. The Atlantic is also under way with a new 50-state tour, The Atlantic Across America , that has already held events in 10 states, addressing some of the most complex issues of our time. Below is Evan Smith’s announcement to staff: I’m excited to let you know that we’ve hired the amazing Jessica Goldstein as our new senior vice president of events. As the second-in-command on our growing team, she’ll oversee the operations, planning, and execution of our robust public programs, working closely with our sales, marketing, design, and CSG colleagues to grow The Atlanti c’s audience and revenue; shine a great, big light on our brand; and—most crucially—bring our journalists and our journalism to stages from coast to coast through The Atlantic Festival, The Atlantic Across America, The Atlantic Summits, and so much more. Jessica comes to us most recently from the Skoll Foundation, where she was managing director of convenings, leading the organization’s global events strategy and directing the Skoll World Forum, a weeklong gathering of heads of state, social entrepreneurs, and civil-society partners. But it’s her reputation at NPR that really precedes her—and makes her the ideal hire in this moment. As senior director and executive producer of Events & Experiential, she spent eight years creating and leading NPR’s live programming, including the Tiny Desk Contest and the How I Built This Summit. Previously she was a senior supervising producer for NPR Music, a senior producer on the science desk, and a producer of audio documentaries known as NPR Radio Expeditions. A native of New York, Jessica is a graduate of the University of Wisconsin at Madison. Jessica believes in the power of storytelling, of sharing ideas and sparking inspiration, which is precisely how we think about our work in the events space. There is no loftier task before us than getting people from divergent backgrounds—great minds who don’t think alike—in a room to listen and talk and continue the conversation after we’re gone. She will bring to bear her decades of experience, her imagination, her creativity, her calm, and her charisma as we expand the ambitious work of the Live team. Press Contacts : Anna Bross and Paul Jackson | press@theatlantic.com

items.title: Boulgou : La 2e édition de « Beguédo School Event’s » place l’éducation au cœur de la lutte contre la migration irrégulière
items.description: Boulgou : La 2e édition de « Beguédo School Event's » place l'éducation au cœur de la lutte contre la migration irrégulière Béguédo, 22 août 2026 (AIB) – Le Président de la délégation spéciale de la commune de Béguédo, le Camarade Moussa W. Ouédraogo, a présidé la 2e édition de « Beguédo School Event's », le samedi 23 août 2026, au Centre culturel ARBI à Dangagou, secteur 04 de Béguédo, pour promouvoir la scolarisation des enfants et sensibiliser sur les risques de la migration irrégulière. L'activité a été organisée par l'Association pour la promotion de l'art et de la culture du Nakambé (APAC-N), en collaboration avec l'Association des ressortissants de Béguédo en Italie (ARBI). Placée sous le thème « Ensemble pour la culture, l'unité et le développement », cette 2e édition a été placée sous le patronage de Naaba Tanga II de Béguédo, sous la présidence du Camarade PDS de la commune de Béguédo, et sous le parrainage de Euro Multi Service, de Procureur Smart Store et de E.Z.I.F. La cérémonie a réuni les autorités locales, les services de l'éducation, les parents d'élèves, les jeunes et les acteurs culturels. Elle a été marquée par des prestations de danses traditionnelle et moderne, du théâtre, un défilé de mode en kokodonda et une opération de plantation d'arbres dans l'enceinte du centre culturel pour reverdir le cadre. L'initiative est portée par le président de l'APAC-N, le Camarade Guillaume Séouni, avec comme invité d'honneur le Camarade Abdoul Salam Bara, président de l'ARBI. Prenant la parole, le Camarade Bara a insisté sur la nécessité d'acquérir une éducation et des compétences avant d'envisager toute aventure migratoire. Pour lui, la scolarisation demeure le socle de l'insertion socio-professionnelle, y compris à l'étranger. « La scolarisation est le meilleur investissement que l'on puisse faire sur son enfant », a-t-il déclaré, invitant les parents à faire de l'éducation une priorité absolue. Il a mis en garde les jeunes contre l'illusion selon laquelle l'école serait inutile pour qui rêve d'Europe, soulignant que l'absence de qualification expose les migrants à des emplois précaires et à diverses formes de vulnérabilité. Le président de l'ARBI a, par ailleurs, plaidé pour la multiplication au Burkina Faso d'activités culturelles et éducatives susceptibles de maintenir le lien entre les enfants restés au pays et les ressortissants vivant à l'étranger. Il a invité les autorités éducatives et les acteurs locaux à accompagner l'initiative en vue de sa pérennisation et de son extension à d'autres communes. Pour sa part, le président de l'APAC-N, le Camarade Guillaume Séouni, a rappelé que le message de l'événement est simple : l'école et la formation préparent l'avenir. Il a remercié l'ARBI pour son appui constant et salué la mobilisation des parents, des jeunes et des bénévoles. « L'école est la clé de l'avenir. Un enfant scolarisé apprend à lire, à écrire, à réfléchir par lui-même et à acquérir des compétences utiles pour toute sa vie », a-t-il soutenu. De son côté, le représentant du coordonnateur provincial de la Culture du Boulgou, le Camarade Ousmane Dabré, a salué la pertinence de l'initiative, tout en déplorant la faible participation des garçons aux activités de teinture du pagne kokodonda. Il a exhorté les parents à encourager davantage les garçons à s'y impliquer, au même titre que les filles. Pour les organisateurs, cette 2e édition qui allie sensibilisation, expression culturelle et engagement citoyen à travers le reboisement, vise à rapprocher les jeunes de l'école et de leur patrimoine culturel, tout en les conscientisant sur les dangers de la migration irrégulière. Ils ont, pour finir, lancé un appel aux autorités locales, aux services de l'éducation, aux établissements scolaires et aux associations de la commune à mutualiser leurs efforts pour garantir la continuité de l'événement. Les organisateurs se sont donné rendez-vous pour la 3e édition, avec l'ambition d'en faire un événement d'envergure provinciale. Agence d'Information du Burkina SM/ata

Trump administration moves to impose more than $100,000 fee for H-1B worker visas
items.description: President Donald Trump’s administration on Monday released a proposed regulation to codify an unprecedented more than $100,000 fee on new H-1B visas for highly skilled foreign workers, that Trump first imposed last year but has been blocked by the courts. The fee first imposed by Trump in a temporary proclamation last year vastly raises the cost of the visas that are heavily relied on in the tech, education and research sectors. A federal judge in June ruled that the fee was illegal and blocked the Trump administration from collecting it. A Boston-based appeals court is reviewing that decision while a different court considers whether a judge in Washington, DC, properly rejected a challenge to the fee by a major business group. Trump’s 2025 proclamation imposing the fee expires in September, one year after it was issued, but directed the US Department of Homeland Security to adopt regulations making it permanent. The proposed $103,265 fee by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), posted online in the Federal Register on Monday to be formally published on Tuesday, kicks off a 30-day public comment period. The rule could be finalised by the end of the year. The H-1B program allows US employers to hire foreign workers with training in specialty fields and offers 65,000 visas annually, with another 20,000 for workers with advanced degrees, approved for three to six years. The order Trump issued last year sharply increased the cost of obtaining some H-1B visas, which had typically come with about $2,000 to $5,000 in fees, depending on various factors. Debate over visa program Trump, a Republican, and other critics of the H-1B program say it is abused by many companies who replace American workers with cheaper foreign labour. But business groups and many individual companies have said the visa program is needed to address a lack of qualified American workers for some jobs and to allow US businesses to recruit top talent. About 70 employers had paid the $100,000 fee on a total of 85 visa applications as of late February, according to court filings. In imposing the fee, Trump invoked the president’s power under federal immigration law to restrict the entry of certain foreign nationals who would be detrimental to US interests. The fee is being challenged by the US Chamber of Commerce, the largest US business lobbying group, Democratic-led states and a coalition of unions and employers. Those lawsuits could be amended to challenge the rule proposed this week once it is finalised. Legal challenges mount The lawsuits claim that Trump’s power to restrict entry does not allow him to override the law that created the H-1B visa program. The states and groups that sued also say that DHS cannot impose fees, taxes or other means to generate revenue for the United States without permission from Congress. The Trump administration has maintained that the fee is not a traditional tax and that courts have little power to question the president’s authority to restrict entry into the country. Amid Trump’s broader immigration crackdown, employers last year registered for about 344,000 H-1B visas, down more than 25 per cent from 2024 and fewer than half of the 794,000 visas sought in 2023, according to data from US Citizenship and Immigration Services. The Trump administration has also ordered enhanced vetting of H-1B applicants and proposed a new visa selection process that would favour higher-skilled and better-paid workers. Earlier in August, DHS in a separate rule added fees of up to $4,500 to applications to extend the stay of H-1B workers or to transfer employees based in other countries to the United States.

items.title: TUC pickets Abuja Continental, says workers treated like slaves
items.description: —Vows to occupy premises till Friday before reviewing situation By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — THE Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC) on Monday picketed the Abuja Continental Hotel, accusing management of violating workers’ fundamental rights and treating employees like “slaves” by denying them the chance to unionize and engage in collective bargaining. TUC officials and members of its affiliates — including the Hotels and Personal Services Senior Staff Association (HAPSSAN) and the National Union of Professional and Allied Staff of Nigeria (NUPSI) — staged a picket that halted activities at the hotel when they converged on the premises. Protesters tried to block the hotel’s entrance and lock its gate, but security staff and some hotel officials pushed back; numerous security operatives were also present on the premises. Speaking during the action, Comrade Nuhu Toro, Secretary-General of the TUC, said the union had exhausted all avenues for dialogue with hotel management before resorting to picketing. He said, “The issue is very clear. The hotel workers are slaves in Abuja Continental, their rights have been violated. They are not allowed to exercise their fundamental human rights and that is why we are here.” He explained that the labour centre had deliberately chosen dialogue before industrial action, revealing that the TUC wrote the hotel management on August 4 to invite it for discussions on how to resolve the dispute peacefully. “But to our surprise, the management of Abuja Continental wrote us back to say, owing to renovation exercise going on, they might not be available to discuss with us until the end of November. “How does that make sense to you? We are talking about workers’ rights being violated. We are talking about workers being treated as slaves, and you are postponing it until the renovation is done. “Invariably, which means by the time they are done with the renovation, all our workers will have died.” Toro explained that the response by the hotel management left the TUC with no option but to escalate the matter, insisting that workers’ rights could not be placed on hold because a renovation exercise was taking place. “It’s against that background that we are here to exercise our fundamental right and press on our demand that they do have a right to unionisation and collective bargaining.” Citing Section 40 of the 1999 Constitution as amended, which guarantees freedom of association, Toro maintained that the workers must be allowed to exercise the right without intimidation or interference as he declared, “That’s why we are here.” The TUC secretary-general said the protest was not intended to shut down the hotel permanently, stressing that the labour centre remained prepared to negotiate with management. “We will be here for this week. From now until Friday, we will be here. We will review it on Friday. If they are ready to talk, we will talk. “But I can assure you that the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria, under the leadership of Comrade Engineer Osifo, is ready to dialogue. That was why we wrote the letter. It’s up to them to come and dialogue with us. “If they want to dialogue right now, we are ready to dialogue with them. But workers are the backbone.” Toro also rejected suggestions that the workers were united against unionisation, following the appearance of some hotel workers carrying banners indicating that they did not want to belong to a trade union. Asked whether the protesters could authoritatively claim to represent all the hotel workers, he said, “Everybody has a right to his opinion. Are they all the workers? Can you authoritatively tell me that they are all the workers? No. So, of course, we don’t expect anything less.” He insisted that the TUC had information indicating that some workers supported the unionisation drive but were afraid to openly identify with the protest. “But I can rest assured you that the workers are members in there. They are resolute. They are ready to join the union and we will ensure that their rights are guaranteed,.” Toro also said the labour centre was not opposed to any meeting initiated by the hotel management, provided the person attending had the authority to negotiate on behalf of the organisation. “We don’t know,” he said when asked about reports of a meeting allegedly called by the management. “We are ready to discuss with anybody. So long as the person has mandate to negotiate with us in good faith on behalf of the management, why not? “We want a peaceful resolution and that’s what we stand for.” The National President of Hotels and Personal Services Senior Staff Association (HAPSSAN), Comrade Iyeh Adegbe accused the hotel of allegedly maintaining an anti-union posture since its takeover by new investors. Adegbe who said the problem was not peculiar to Abuja Continental, alleging that a similar situation existed at the Continental Hotel in Lagos, recalled that the former Sheraton Hotel, which the current investors took over, had an active union structure before the COVID-19 pandemic. “After COVID-19 and these people took over as a new investor, they told their employees that union is a taboo and they have established this place like a slave camp,” he alleged. According to him, workers had been denied access to proper conditions of service and the right to freely associate. He said HAPSSAN and NUPSI had written several letters to the management seeking dialogue, but the letters failed to yield the desired result “That was why we escalated to the labour centre, which is the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria,” he said. Adegbe added that the management’s decision to defer discussions until November was unacceptable to organised labour. “That is the reason why you see the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria coming to say that what people are saying about them is true and is correct. Our mandate is to defend workers anywhere in Nigeria.” However, some workers seconded to the hotel by outsourcing companies have dissociated themselves from the picketing. The workers through their spokesman, Samuel Esiakpoyere, said the industrial action did not represent their interests, insisting that they had deliberately chosen not to participate. The workers cited Section 40 of the Constitution, arguing that employees were free to decide whether or not to belong to a trade union. They also cited Section 12 of the TUC Constitution, which they said recognises the voluntary nature of union membership. “We can choose to join or not. It’s not by force,” the workers said, insisting that they receive their salaries and benefits regularly and enjoy HMO and other welfare packages. They also said the hotel operates an open-door policy and provides channels through which workers can raise concerns. “We are satisfied with how we currently engage with Abuja Continental Hotel management and believe our interests are being adequately protected. Our decision not to participate in any picketing is deliberate,” they said. But the TUC has rejected the suggestion that the workers’ public position settles the dispute, insisting that the fundamental issue is whether workers are genuinely free to organise and bargain collectively. Addressing the workers of Abuja Continental Hotel who mounted top of the Hotel’s security post with banners dissociating themselves from the picketing, the National Union of Professional and Allied Staff of Nigeria (NUPSI), Comrade Martin Egbanubi said the TUC and it’s affiliates were not at the Hotel to joke. “We are here to enforce the law, because the law has provided that workers anywhere have the right to work and workers of Abuja Continental Hotel must belong to trade unions. “We don’t want any workers here to work under preparation, under a condition that is not protected by law and that is why we are here. So make sure that as Nigerian citizens working here, you have the right, fundamental right, protection of your job, protection of your wage, protection of your condition of service, your freedom must also be guaranteed. “As you see how we work in several organizations across the economy, several sectors of Nigeria’s economy we are gathered here because we are free and that is why we are free to exercise our freedom in our respective places of work. “We are here not only in solidarity with the oppressed workers of Abuja Continental Hotel, but also to enforce their fundamental rights. “Their fundamental right to collective behavior, their fundamental right to job security, their fundamental right to wage protection, their fundamental right to enjoy all conditions of work in line with standard level laws.” The post TUC pickets Abuja Continental, says workers treated like slaves appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ogou/Commerce: Les acteurs économiques du Méridionnal outillés sur les réformes commerciales à Atakpamé
items.description: Atakpamé, 24 août (ATOP) – Un atelier de sensibilisation et de partage d’informations sur les instruments majeurs de facilitation du commerce et de modernisation de l’économie togolaise se tient les 24 et 25 août à Atakpamé. Organisée par le ministère délégué chargé du Commerce et du Contrôle de la Qualité sous l’égide du Ministère de l’Économie et de la Veille stratégique, cette rencontre réunit une centaine de participants des régions des Plateaux, Maritime et du Grand Lomé, incluant des parlementaires notamment députés et sénateurs, des élus consulaires ainsi que des opérateurs économiques. L’objectif principal est de favoriser une appropriation optimale des mécanismes du commerce international. Il s’agit d’amener les acteurs économiques à maîtriser les outils numériques et réglementaires nécessaires pour conquérir de nouveaux marchés et faire du commerce un levier de croissance, de création d’emplois décents et de prospérité nationale. Quatre axes prioritaires meubleront les échanges, notamment, le Guichet unique du commerce extérieur (GUCE), la Zone de libre-échange continentale africaine (ZLECAf), la Solution automatisée de marquage (SAM) des produits, et le commerce électronique à travers la plateforme « Togo Trade Portal ». Le secrétaire général du ministère chargé du Commerce, Comlan Yakpey, a précisé que ces réformes structurelles traduisent la vision du Président du Conseil, Faure Gnassingbé, visant à faire du Togo un hub logistique, commercial et d’investissement de référence. « Le Guichet unique simplifie et dématérialise les procédures pour réduire les délais et les coûts, tandis que le marquage automatisé garantit la traçabilité des produits, luttant ainsi contre la fraude et la concurrence déloyale. Conjugués aux opportunités de la ZLECAf et au commerce électronique, ces instruments renforcent la compétitivité de nos entreprises, notamment des TPME », a-t-il affirmé. Il a appelé à une synergie accrue entre pouvoirs publics, élus et secteur privé. Le secrétaire général du gouvernorat, Vidoute Aimé Koffi, a exprimé sa gratitude au gouvernement pour les actions menées en faveur du développement socio-économique régional. ATOP/AY/KKT/SED

items.title: Plateau police ban Keke operations in Jos, Bukuru for Eid Maulud
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — The Plateau State Police Command has announced a temporary ban on the operation of commercial tricycles, popularly known as Keke NAPEP, in the Jos-Bukuru metropolis and other major towns across the state during the Eid El Maulud celebration. The command said the restriction would take effect on Tuesday as part of measures to ensure a peaceful and orderly celebration. In a statement issued by the Police Public Relations Officer, PPRO, SP Alfred Alabo, on Monday, the command said the measure was aimed at enhancing security and public safety during the celebration. According to the statement, the restriction is being implemented in collaboration with other security agencies and relevant stakeholders to ensure a hitch-free Eid Maulud celebration. The Commissioner of Police, CP Ayodeji Faniyan, urged tricycle operators and members of the public to comply with the directive, assuring residents that adequate personnel would be deployed to major roads, prayer grounds and other public places. He said the deployment was intended to maintain law and order before, during and after the celebration. The CP also warned police personnel against using the temporary restriction as an avenue for extortion, directing members of the public not to give money to any officer who demands payment from apprehended tricycle operators. “Any officer found engaging in such acts will be severely dealt with in accordance with Police regulations,” the statement quoted the CP as saying. The command urged anyone confronted with an extortion attempt or other misconduct by police personnel to report the incident through the designated emergency lines. It also appealed to parents and guardians to caution their children and wards against acts capable of disrupting public peace during the Eid Maulud celebration. The command further clarified that the existing ban on motorcycles, popularly known as Okada, remains in force within Jos and Bukuru metropolis and other areas covered by the Jos Master Plan. It advised residents to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious movements or activities during the celebration. The post Plateau police ban Keke operations in Jos, Bukuru for Eid Maulud appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ECC approves bonded storage of imported petroleum products
items.description: ISLAMABAD: In view of recent supply disruptions following the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, the government on Monday formally approved allowing foreign fuel suppliers to establish bonded storage facilities in Pakistan at their own expense for multiple purposes, including re-export and supplies to the domestic market. Subject to formal ratification by the federal cabinet, the new policy guidelines on “Import on Foreign Supplier’s Account through Customs Bonded Storage Facilities” will come into force immediately. The guidelines have been pending since June 2023. The guidelines were approved at a meeting of the federal cabinet’s Economic Coordination Committee (ECC), chaired by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb. The ECC “approved a summary with [the] proposal of the Petroleum Division to allow [the] import of petroleum products on foreign suppliers’ account through Customs bonded storage facilities,” a statement issued after the meeting said. “The proposal focused on the development and strengthening of the key pillars of the country’s energy security architecture in the oil and gas sector, including indigenisation, the development of strategic petroleum reserves and the promotion of Customs bonded storage facilities to ensure a resilient and sustainable petroleum supply chain,” an official statement issued after the meeting said. The recent disruptions in the strategic waterway prompted the government to examine supply-chain vulnerabilities in the context of national energy security. The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) had opposed the policy, citing its own collection and monitoring challenges, but almost all other stakeholders supported the petroleum minister’s proposal to proceed with bonded warehouses and engage with key suppliers in the Middle East. The policy guidelines cleared by the ECC would cover the import of all grades of crude oil, motor spirit (petrol), high-speed diesel (HSD), jet fuel, furnace oil, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and liquefied natural gas (LNG) on foreign suppliers’ accounts through Customs bonded storage facilities in Pakistan. The imports would be subject to the product specifications approved by Ogra. The policy would not, however, cover goods subject to international sanctions binding on Pakistan or those listed in the Negative List of the Import Policy Order, 2022. The policy covers domestic sales to oil marketing companies (OMCs) and refineries. Foreign suppliers would be able to maintain bonded inventories for local sale at private and public bonded storage terminals, including dedicated storage terminals, at approved locations such as Port Qasim Authority, KPT/Keamari, Hub and Gwadar Port, as well as any other designated ports, including Mahmood Kot and Machike, Sheikhupura. For imports into bonded storage and re-export, both private and public bonded storage terminals at ports would be approved locations, including those at Port Qasim Authority, KPT/Keamari, Hub and Gwadar Port, as well as any other designated ports, subject to compliance with the relevant laws and regulations of the respective port, marine and other regulatory authorities. Foreign suppliers, through their consignees, would have access to the national petroleum pipeline network to move bonded inventory from approved port-based locations to inland locations — such as Mahmood Kot and Machike, Sheikhupura — for local sale to licensed OMCs and refineries. No duty or tax would be triggered by such bonded pipeline movements, while goods declaration (GD) filing requirements would apply. These guidelines will not affect or alter the existing regime for imports of petroleum products by licensed OMCs and refineries on their own account. The existing OMC import regime will continue unchanged and in parallel with this initiative. Foreign suppliers, through their consignees, will be allowed to maintain inventories of crude oil and other aforementioned products in private and public bonded storage facilities, including dedicated storage terminals. Meanwhile, foreign suppliers or their consignees will have the option to develop their own dedicated storage infrastructure or utilise private or public bonded warehouse facilities and dedicated storage terminals, subject to the relevant regulatory approvals under the Customs Act, 1969 and from the relevant port authorities. The consignee’s bonded storage facility — whether a public bonded warehouse, private bonded warehouse or dedicated storage terminal — will have to be licensed by Customs after fulfilling the requirements for operating as a bonded warehouse. Additionally, they will not be required to register with the FBR under the Sales Tax Act, 1990, as a condition for commencing operations under this policy. For domestic sales of bonded goods to OMCs, all sales tax obligations — including registration as an importer under the Sales Tax Act, 1990, filing of returns and payment of sales tax — would apply to and rest solely with the OMC or refinery as the importer of record at ex-bonding. The foreign supplier and the consignee would have no sales tax registration requirement, return-filing obligation or liability to pay sales tax in respect of domestic sales. Under the policy guidelines, concessions would be granted to the consignee and the foreign supplier to ensure that they remain tax-neutral in Pakistan in respect of bonded storage, blending, trading and re-export operations. At the time of storing goods received under the scheme, consignees would not be required to file an Electronic Import Form (EIF) with their GD for in-bonding. Several system changes would be required to operationalise this arrangement, including a joint State Bank-FBR circular enabling multiple partial EIFs to be drawn against a single in-bond cargo GD, and configuring the Web-Based One Customs (WeBOC) system to track cumulative ex-bonded quantities and accept NOC-based ex-bond GDs. The consignee may sell bonded goods to licensed purchasers in foreign currency, with the letter of credit or open contract in the name of the foreign supplier and payment made directly into its foreign bank account through an authorised dealer, in accordance with applicable foreign exchange regulations. Moreover, the sale and purchase of goods between the foreign supplier and Pakistani purchasers would be conducted on a purely commercial basis, without any liability on the part of the government. Upon the domestic sale of bonded goods, the consignee shall issue a no-objection certificate for the change of ownership. The OMC or refinery shall file the ex-bond GD, submit the Electronic Import Form through its designated scheduled bank, and pay all applicable customs duty, sales tax and other charges at the rates applicable at the time of ex-bonding. The FBR shall allow the movement of duty-paid products through pipelines or any other mode of transportation and facilitate local purchasers in making input and output tax adjustments. This policy will not restrict or alter the import rights of OMCs and refineries under the Product Review Meeting (PRM) framework. Upon importation into Pakistan and any subsequent movement between bonded warehouses without a sale, the consignee shall file the in-bond GD. Upon sale to a local purchaser, the purchaser shall immediately file the relevant ex-bond GD. Regarding pricing, Ogra-regulated prices will apply solely to the onward sale of petroleum products in the country by purchasers from bonded storage and will not restrict the international oil supplier’s unconditional right to re-export bonded goods at any time. Therefore, pricing obligations under Ogra notifications will apply to local purchasers and not to the foreign supplier or the consignee. Foreign suppliers will retain full pricing flexibility to sell bonded petroleum products to local OMCs and refineries at commercially negotiated prices. Such prices will not be subject to Ogra price notifications. The customs value of imported goods, for the purposes of assessing applicable customs duties, taxes, levies and other statutory charges, shall be the transaction value prevailing at the time of sale to the local purchaser in Pakistan. For the avoidance of doubt, if the sale by the consignee and ex-bonding by the local purchaser occur simultaneously, the transaction value applicable on the date of filing the ex-bond GD shall apply. The government will have the option to requisition bonded products in an emergency, but only where the government has officially declared a formal emergency, including war, armed conflict, a major natural disaster or a complete and documented collapse of domestic supply. Emergency requisitioning would not apply to routine energy shortages, price fluctuations, geopolitical events that do not cause supply disruptions or government procurement preferences. The government will have the right to request access to the consignee’s bonded petroleum stocks physically present at all approved bonded storage locations at the time of the request. In such cases, requisitioned goods shall be compensated at the prevailing international market price on the date of requisition, determined by reference to the weekly average of the published Platts price assessment for the relevant product and delivery point. Payment shall be made in any foreign currency within 15 calendar days of delivery. The government shall submit a formal requisition notice specifying the volume, product and delivery point. However, requisitioned stocks shall be purchased and removed within 14 days of the request. No authority may require the consignee to hold stocks in reserve. Additionally, the consignee shall report the stocks held at each approved bonded storage location to Ogra on a daily basis, disaggregated by product grade, in a format prescribed by the regulator and entered into a central regulatory database accessible to the relevant regulators. This reporting obligation shall apply to all products regulated by Ogra and covered by this policy, as well as all approved bonded storage locations.

items.title: Trump govt proposes $103k fee for skilled worker visa
items.description: US President Donald Trump’s administration on Monday moved to impose a more than $100,000 fee on employers hiring foreign workers through a highly-skilled visa program, after facing a legal setback in an earlier effort. The $103,265 fee for H-1B visas would serve as a “revenue mechanism” to recoup the costs of administering the lawful immigration system, the Department of Homeland Security said in its new proposed rule. The Trump administration has argued the visa program has been exploited to replace, rather than supplement, American workers — and in September 2025 issued a presidential proclamation imposing a $100,000 fee to combat what it called “systemic abuse.” But a federal judge in June blocked that order, siding with 20 Democratic-led states in a lawsuit that contended the fee constituted an unlawful tax that bypassed Congressional authority. Another federal judge in December 2025 upheld the same action, finding the president had “broad statutory authority” to address “a problem he perceives to be a matter of economic and national security,” and that ruling is being appealed. In the new proposal, the administration leans more heavily on cost-based arguments, saying it needs to make up the costs of its agencies including US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), Customs and Border Protection (CBP), Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). However, it also acknowledges it would have what it calls an “indirect” benefit: “US employers, if required to pay an additional $103,265 fee when filing an H-1B cap-subject petition, would be less likely to hire an H-1B worker over a qualified and highly-skilled American.” And it says the new proposed fee “would be in addition to any other applicable fees or payments,” including the presidential proclamation that is under legal review — meaning if the original $100,000 fee is allowed to go ahead, the new payment would be stacked on top. Congress created the H-1B program in 1990, and the US currently awards 85,000 H-1B visas per year. Past holders of H-1B visas include several prominent tech executives, including SpaceX’s Elon Musk and Google CEO Sundar Pichai. Critics say the new rules will leave critical shortages in fields including medical, engineering and sciences. The post Trump govt proposes $103k fee for skilled worker visa appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Edo Assembly converts ex-Speaker’s resignation to impeachment
items.description: ​‌‍‍‍The Edo House of Assembly, on Monday, rejected the purported resignation of former Speaker, Blessing Agbebaku. The House, instead, converted the resignation to impeachment during plenary session in Benin. Moving the motion for Agbebaku’s impeachment, the Majority Leader, Sunday Ojezele, said the alleged resignation letter was not received by the House. Ojezele, who represents Esan South-East, said that the verbal resignation process “was unknown to parliamentary practices and did not conform with parliamentary procedures”. He urged members to support the impeachment of the ex-speaker. A majority of the members supported the motion for Agbebaku’s impeachment. Ojezele subsequently presented the impeachment letter to the Clerk, Mr Yahaya Omogbai, for onward transmission to the Speaker, Yekini Idiaye. In a remark, the speaker condemned what he described as Agbebaku’s “worrisome and unwarranted attitude” and reiterated that he remained suspended. Idiaye directed Agbebaku to return all the House property in his possession on or before Friday. He warned that law enforcement agencies would be engaged, should he fail to comply. The House also passed two key bills that were designed to strengthen financial autonomy and institutional independence in the state. The first pass was a bill for a Law to Amend the Edo State House of Assembly Fund Management Law 2023. The second was a bill for a Law to Amend the Edo State Judiciary Financial Autonomy Law 2023, after resolving into a committee of the whole. Ojezele reiterated that strengthening institutions and government agencies would help curb corruption and fraud while safeguarding institutional autonomy. The Speaker directed the clerk to transmit clean copies of both bills to Gov. Monday Okpebholo for assent. The House also confirmed Mr Ambrose Ayewoh-Oyakhilomen, who hails from Esan North-East, as the Deputy Chairman of the Edo State Universal Basic Education Board. The House, thereafter, adjourned its sitting until Wednesday The post Edo Assembly converts ex-Speaker’s resignation to impeachment appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Drame de Dar-es-Salam : trois enfants de Ciré Kallo décédés, deux autres rescapés à Donka
items.description: La famille Kallo, durement frappée par l’éboulement meurtrier de Dar-es-Salam, connaît une évolution de son bilan. Alors que Ciré Kallo pensait avoir perdu ses cinq enfants, trois sont finalement décédés et deux autres ont été retrouvés vivants. Les deux rescapés, une fille et le dernier garçon de la famille, sont actuellement hospitalisés au CHU Donka, où ils reçoivent des soins. L’information a été confirmée ce lundi par le maire de Gbessia, Mamadou Saliou Fofana, après une visite à l’hôpital. « Madame Kallo, que j’ai moi-même rencontrée hier, avait perdu son mari et ses cinq enfants. On a constaté aujourd’hui que, parmi ces cinq enfants, il y en a deux qui vivent encore et qui sont actuellement hospitalisés à l’hôpital Donka : une fille et le dernier, un garçon. Pour le moment, au lieu de cinq enfants qui ont perdu la vie, ils sont trois. Les deux autres sont vivants, tout comme leur maman. C’est seulement le papa et deux autres enfants qui ont perdu la vie », a-t-il expliqué. Selon l’élu local, l’état de santé des deux enfants est désormais stable, après une situation jugée préoccupante au lendemain du drame. « L’état des enfants est stable. Les médecins nous ont dit qu’aujourd’hui, leur état est vraiment stable. Hier, c’était un peu compliqué, mais nous avons même échangé avec les enfants qui, d’ailleurs, parlent très bien. En les voyant, ils sont vraiment en bonne forme », a-t-il rassuré. Après avoir perdu son mari et trois de ses enfants, Ciré Kallo peut ainsi compter sur la survie de ses deux autres enfants, actuellement sous surveillance médicale au CHU Donka. Mayi CISSÉ L’article Drame de Dar-es-Salam : trois enfants de Ciré Kallo décédés, deux autres rescapés à Donka est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: NPP Ahafo Region rebuts Asunafo North MCE, outlines gains of administrative Region’s creation
items.description: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) Communications Directorate in the Ahafo Region has strongly criticised the Municipal Chief Executive (MCE) for Asunafo North, Joseph Akparibo, over statements attributed to him describing the creation of the Ahafo Region as a “useless” undertaking. In a press engagement addressed by Regional Communications Officer Alfred Asiedu, the NPP demanded an apology from the MCE to the people and chiefs of the Ahafo Region for his disrespectful comments. The party warned that failure to issue an apology would spark public demonstrations demanding his immediate resignation or the termination of his appointment by President John Mahama. He emphasized that the creation of the region in 2019 under the Akufo-Addo/Bawumia administration successfully fulfilled a long-standing demand for administrative decentralization and accelerated local development. To counter the MCE’s claims, the party highlighted major achievements and economic gains realized since achieving regional status: Infrastructure Expansion: Completed projects such as the Bechem-Techimantia-Akumadan road and ongoing work on the Tepa-Goaso road have improved inter-regional transport. Justice delivery has also expanded through a new High Court in Goaso and a District Court in Hwidiem. Educational and Health Initiatives: Key developments include the proposed Akrodie STEM University (with a campus at Mim), the UMaT satellite campus at Kenyasi No.2, inclusion in the Secondary Cities Project (delivering a modern market in Goaso), and plans for a regional hospital. Economic Growth and IGF Increase: Establishing Goaso as the regional capital has boosted local commerce, real estate, and hospitality, significantly raising the Internally Generated Funds (IGF) of the Asunafo North Municipal Assembly. Employment Creation: Decentralized public institutions, including regional directorates for education, health, agriculture, and security, have generated hundreds of direct civil service jobs and indirect economic opportunities. Enhanced Security: Dedicated regional command structures for the Police, Fire, and Immigration services have bolstered local law enforcement and public safety. International Partnerships: Under regional leadership, formal diplomatic ties were forged with several foreign embassies, including China, Germany, and South Korea to market local investment prospects in agriculture and mining. The NPP urged officials in the Ahafo to focus on building upon the region’s expanding economic foundation rather than dismissing the tangible progress achieved since 2019.

items.title: Lacs : Les jeunes édifiés sur la prévention des violences basées sur le genre
items.description: Lomé, 24 août (ATOP) – Les jeunes de la commune Lacs 1 ont été sensibilisés, sur la prévention et la réponse aux Violences basées sur le genre (VBG), le vendredi 21 août à Aného. Cette activité est à l’actif du Centre de lecture et d’animation culturelle d’Aného (CLAC-Aného) et s’inscrit dans le cadre de la célébration en différé de la journée internationale de la jeunesse, édition 2026. Elle vise à promouvoir l’engagement des jeunes dans le développement durable, de la cohésion sociale et de la paix. La rencontre a permis d’outiller les jeunes sur la prévention et les réponses aux VBG. La séance a été animée par la responsable de l’action sociale auprès de l’hôpital psychiatrique de Zébé-Aného, Mme Goza Ablavi Ida. Cette dernière a entretenu l’assistance sur le genre, les différentes formes de violences, notamment violences physiques, psychologiques, sexuelles, économiques et leur impact sur les jeunes. La conférencière a relevé les causes des VBG et insisté sur leurs conséquences, entre autres, la mort, les grossesses précoces et non désirées, l’abandon scolaire. Elle a invité l’assistance et les victimes à dénoncer en cas de VBG. Mme Goza a instruit ses interlocuteurs sur les mécanismes de signalisation, tels que le numéro vert 8284, la gendarmerie, la police, les services sociaux, les centres d’écoute, la justice, les parents et les encadrants. Elle a abordé aussi la législation togolaise et les droits des victimes. Le responsable du CLAC-Aného, Lémou Toyi, conseiller de jeunesse, a invité les jeunes à la discipline sexuelle en se maitrisant et se contrôlant pour éviter de se créer des problèmes. Il a exhorté les jeunes filles à revoir leur habillement et à éviter de se retrouver seules à des endroits dangereux. La journée internationale de la jeunesse est observée chaque 12 août. Elle est axée cette année au plan national sur le thème « Jeunesse togolaise : Des réalités locales, une même ambition de développement ». ATOP/DK/MD/BV

items.title: Old Tafo disability fund support shifts focus from handouts to livelihoods
items.description: For Owusu Michael, a phone repairer in Tafo, a small piece of equipment could change how much work he is able to take on each day. He has been given a phone repair equipment under the latest disbursement of the Disability Fund by the Old Tafo Municipal Assembly in the Ashanti region. The equipment, he says, will allow him to work faster and improve his livelihood. “The phone repair tool will help me do more work in a day than I was able to do before. It will help improve my standard of living,” he said. Michael is one of 31 persons with disabilities receiving support under the second disbursement of the fund in 2026. The intervention, according to the Old Tafo Municipal Assembly, is intended to move beyond immediate assistance and help beneficiaries establish or strengthen livelihoods. At a ceremony in the municipality, the Municipal Chief Executive, Abubakar Sadiq, said the support should be seen as an investment in the ability of persons with disabilities to participate in economic life. “Persons with disabilities are not merely recipients of social support. They are citizens with skills, talents, aspirations and the capacity to contribute significantly to the development of their families, communities and our municipality.” The assembly says 33 persons with disabilities received educational and medical support in July 2026. The latest beneficiaries are receiving items and support for activities including poultry, onion farming, trading, food-related businesses and other enterprises. The MCE said the government’s decision to increase the allocation for persons with disabilities under the District Assemblies Common Fund from three per cent to five per cent in 2026 had created greater room for assemblies to respond to the needs of beneficiaries. “The government’s decision to increase the allocation for persons with disabilities under the District Assemblies Common Fund from 3% to 5% in 2026 is therefore a significant step towards strengthening disability inclusion and economic empowerment.” For the beneficiaries, the value of the intervention lies in what the items can enable them to do. Sulemana Issaka runs a small container business where he sells tea, indomie and other items. He received a freezer and says it could allow him to expand into selling chilled water and drinks. “The freezer I have received will enable me to expand my business by selling water and drinks.” He said the support came unexpectedly. “I am very grateful and thankful for what I have received today. I was not expecting it at all.” The Social Welfare Director, Anita Donkor, said the items were not selected simply for distribution. She said the beneficiaries first made requests, after which the department and the Disability Fund Management Committee conducted needs assessments to determine whether the requested items were appropriate for their intended livelihoods. “We are supposed to conduct needs assessments to ensure that the items the beneficiaries request are appropriate and are what they really need to enhance their livelihoods.” In some cases, she said, the assessment led beneficiaries to change their initial requests. In others, the assessment confirmed that what had been requested was suitable. But Ms Donkor says receiving the items is only the beginning. “Don’t keep them in your household. Make sure you use the items, and the profits you are going to get from them, don’t spend them.” She urged beneficiaries to reinvest their earnings into their businesses rather than consume the initial gains. “When you get money from the things you sell, keep it and use it to buy more items when your stock is finished, so that your investment or business can progress.” From training to a new opportunity For Michael, the support brings back memories of an earlier opportunity that helped him develop his skills. He said he attended a phone repair training programme organised by RLG in Sunyani during the era of the late President John Evans Fiifi Atta Mills, where he received a blower and GH¢1,000. The latest support, he believes, could further improve his work. “The items given to us today will be of great help to us especially me. I am a phone repairer and me given a phone microscope will help me do more work in a day than I was used to doing before receiving this machine.” He expressed gratitude to the MCE and President John Dramani Mahama. The Old Tafo Municipal Assembly says there are 618 registered persons with disabilities in the municipality. The MCE acknowledged that the 31 people receiving support represent only a portion of those who may require assistance. He said the assembly would continue, within available resources and relevant guidelines, to reach eligible beneficiaries. “Our ambition is not simply to distribute support. It is to create an environment where persons with disabilities can work, earn, learn, build businesses, support their families and participate fully in community life.” The assembly also plans to involve traditional authorities, community leaders and disability organisations in the process. The MCE said the Department of Social Welfare and Community Development and the Disability Fund Management Committee would continue monitoring the use of the support. He said the success of the fund should ultimately be judged not by the number of items distributed but by what beneficiaries achieve with them. “Our ultimate objective should be to move from dependency to empowerment, from vulnerability to resilience, and from assistance to sustainable livelihoods.” For Michael and Issaka, that transition has already begun with equipment they believe can help them earn more. For the assembly, the bigger challenge now is ensuring that the support translates into businesses that survive, grow and improve the lives of the people it was intended to serve.
